  • Identificación de oportunidades de automatización y posibles aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial agéntica en procesos tecnológicos.


Esta posición representa una oportunidad para profesionales con experiencia en Java que quieran ampliar su trayectoria hacia la integración de sistemas, el troubleshooting especializado, la consultoría técnica y la tecnología financiera.

About Limble

At Limble we empower the unsung heroes who support the world. We’re revolutionizing the way businesses manage their maintenance operations by providing a comprehensive suite of software solutions that empower organizations to optimize asset performance and drive operational excellence. About the Role

Integrations and technology partnerships are central to how Limble fits into our customers' broader operational stack. This role fully owns that function. You'll decide which technology partners are worth pursuing, recruit the ones that fill gaps in our ecosystem, and turn those relationships into integrations customers adopt and partners actively co-market.

You'll be the front door for inbound partner requests, the voice of the partner ecosystem in product conversations, and the person who carries a partnership from first conversation through signed agreement, launch, and activation. Own technology partner strategy and the integration roadmap

Company: GoTo TelemedLocation: Fully Remote (United States)Employment Type: Full-Time, Part-Time, or PRNCompensation: $38.00 – $52.00 per hourDepartment: Preventive Oral Health & Clinical Triage

Role Overview

GoTo Telemed is seeking a Registered Dental Hygienist (RDH) to join our nationwide virtual healthcare team. In this fully remote position, you will serve as a frontline care coordinator, delivering preventive oral care education, patient triage, and nutritional counseling. Working collaboratively with licensed GoTo Telemed dentists under collaborative practice agreements, you will help patients assess caries and periodontal risks, understand post-treatment recovery plans, and establish healthy home preventive habits without the physical wear-and-tear of traditional chairside scaling.

Key Responsibilities

  • Preventive Guidance: Provide live, one-on-one virtual patient education on home preventive care, biofilm control, and oral hygiene techniques.
  • Risk Assessment: Administer structured caries risk assessments (CAMBRA) and periodontal screening questionnaires via digital intake forms and live video.
  • Wellness Counseling: Deliver individualized counseling focusing on dietary factors, dry mouth management, and tobacco cessation (CDT D9993).
  • Clinical Triage & Store-and-Forward Prep: Monitor incoming patient messages and intraoral photo uploads; identify acute symptoms, assist in gathering clinical data for CDT D9996 asynchronous review, and escalate complex pathology to the supervising dentist.
  • Post-Operative Support: Conduct structured follow-up check-ins after routine or surgical dental treatments to review comfort, healing, and home-care compliance.
  • Patient Navigation: Guide patients through systematic intraoral photo capture using their smartphones to support early detection and telehealth diagnostics.
  • Documentation: Record all assessments and patient interactions in our cloud-based EHR in strict compliance with HIPAA and state recordkeeping laws.

Minimum Qualifications & Requirements

  • Degree in Dental Hygiene from an institution accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation (CODA).
  • Active, unencumbered Dental Hygiene license issued by a U.S. state dental board (multi-state licensure or residence in a collaborative practice state is highly preferred).
  • Clear understanding of dental hygiene scope boundaries and collaborative practice agreements.
  • Dedicated, private, and quiet home office environment meeting HIPAA privacy standards, equipped with high-speed internet.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive hourly compensation ($38.00 – $52.00/hr) with transparent payroll processing.
  • 100% remote flexibility with customizable scheduling blocks.
  • Comprehensive onboarding and training covering digital health workflows and teledentistry triage protocols.
  • Free access to our proprietary cloud-based EHR tools, scheduling software, and virtual communication platforms.

About the company

Omilia is a leader in Conversational AI. Our cloud platform powers natural, human-like customer conversations over voice and chat for some of the largest enterprises in banking, insurance, telecommunications and hospitality, handling hundreds of millions of interactions a year. We build our own deep tech across the stack, from speech recognition and natural language understanding to dialog management, and we integrate natively with the major CCaaS platforms. We are a company of roughly 500 people, distributed across Europe and North America, in the middle of an ambitious platform modernization program: Kubernetes everywhere, autoscaling for every service, a next generation observability stack, and AI woven through our own engineering lifecycle.

Role Purpose

The Solution Consultant a senior individual contributor who serves as the primary technical authority in Account Executive-led sales cycles within an assigned region or global segment. The role bridges commercial and technical disciplines — owning the pre-sales technical motion from discovery through to proof of concept and proposal, while acting as a trusted advisor to strategic prospects and customers within an assigned region or global segment. Operating in close partnership with Account Executives and Account Managers, the SC is accountable for technical win rates, solution quality, and the integrity of commitments made to customers before contract signature.

Accountabilities

  • Own the technical pre-sales motion for certain new-logo deals within the assigned region or global segment — from initial discovery and architecture assessment through solution design, proof of concept, High Level Effort Estimate, RFP/RFI response, and technical close.
  • Serve as the definitive technical authority on Omilia's platform for certain deals within the assigned region or global segment — ensuring that all solution proposals are architecturally sound, technically deliverable, and accurately scoped before commercial commitments are made.
  • Build and maintain trusted advisor relationships with technical decision-makers and enterprise architects at strategic prospect and customer organisations, positioning Omilia as the platform of choice for contact centre AI transformation.
  • Drive technical win rates across the assigned region or global segment by developing and executing differentiated solution narratives that directly address each prospect's environment, constraints, and automation objectives.
  • Collaborate with Demo Engineers within the assigned region or Global Segment to ensure all solution narratives are substantiated by impactful demos
  • Ensure the integrity of RFP and RFI responses for certain opportunities within the assigned region or global segment — owning the technical sections end-to-end and coordinating cross-functional input from Product, Engineering, Security, and Professional Services.
  • Maintain deep, current knowledge of the competitive landscape — including legacy IVR platforms and emerging conversational AI vendors

Key Responsibilities

Technical Discovery and Solution Design

  • Lead structured technical discovery engagements with certain deals within the assigned segment or region — mapping current-state technical architecture, identifying automation gaps, quantifying business impact, and designing Omilia-based solutions that address the customer's specific environment, integration landscape, and regulatory constraints.
  • Conduct in-depth architecture assessments covering telephony infrastructure, CRM and backend system integrations, data flows, security and compliance requirements, and channel strategy — producing a technically grounded solution design that forms the basis for scoping, pricing, and contractual commitments.
  • Develop tailored solution proposals and technical response documents that map Omilia's platform capabilities (OCP, miniApps, Pathfinder, CoPilot, TalkGuard, OptimizeIQ) to each prospect's identified use cases, business outcomes, and technical environment.

Product Demonstrations and Proof of Concept

  • Collaborate with Demo Engineers to design, configure, and deliver highly customised product demonstrations and proof-of-concept (POC) engagements for strategic accounts — moving beyond standard demo scripts to build scenario-specific flows that reflect the prospect's actual customer interactions, industry context, and business language.
  • Own the full POC lifecycle for certain deals within the assigned segment or region — defining success criteria in alignment with the prospect and Account Executive, coordinating internal resources (Professional Services, Engineering) for POC delivery, and presenting results with a clear ROI and deployment readiness narrative.
  • Master the Omilia demo suite across the full product portfolio and maintain demo environments that reflect current platform capabilities, recent product releases, and the most common use cases across verticals (banking, insurance, healthcare, utilities, telecommunications).

RFP and RFI Management

  • Own the technical response to RFPs and RFIs for certain deals within the assigned segment or region — writing and structuring all technical sections, coordinating input from Security, Compliance, Product, and Engineering, and ensuring that responses accurately represent Omilia's capabilities and delivery commitments.
  • Critically evaluate the technical sustainability and delivery risk of each strategic sales opportunities prior to commercial commitment — flagging architectural mismatches, integration complexity, unsupported requirements, or resourcing risks to Sales and Professional Services leadership.
  • Maintain a library of reusable RFP response content, technical answer repositories, and solution templates for use cases common to the assigned region or global segment — continuously updating these assets as the platform evolves.

Technical Advisory and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the sales cycle — engaging IT architects, platform owners, security teams, and C-level technology stakeholders with credibility and depth, addressing objections with evidence-based responses and forward-looking platform context.
  • Proactively identify and address technical objections, integration concerns, and compliance questions early in the sales cycle — building the technical confidence and internal sponsorship necessary to accelerate deal progression and reduce late-stage risk.
  • Conduct technical benefits assessments that quantify the value of Omilia's platform in terms directly relevant to the prospect's business — call deflection rates, AHT reduction, CSAT improvement, agent cost savings, and compliance risk mitigation.

Competitive Positioning

  • Maintain current, detailed knowledge of competing platforms across IVR, CCaaS, and conversational AI categories — including Nuance/Microsoft, Google CCAI, Amazon Connect, Genesys, Avaya, Five9, and NICE inContact — and develop technically rigorous competitive battle cards and displacement strategies Participate in competitive bake-offs and technical evaluations, positioning Omilia's architectural advantages, NLU accuracy, enterprise-grade security posture, and deployment flexibility against incumbent and emerging alternatives.

Cross-functional Collaboration and Internal Contribution

  • Work in close alignment with Account Executives and Account Managers on strategic accounts — providing technical qualification, deal strategy input, and stakeholder mapping support throughout the sales cycle.
  • Collaborate with Professional Services during the transition from pre-sales to delivery — ensuring that technical commitments, integration requirements, and POC outcomes are fully documented and handed over with sufficient context for successful implementation.
  • Maintain accurate records of technical engagement activity, POC status, RFP pipelines, and solution configurations in Salesforce and internal knowledge systems.

Travel

  • Travel within the EU (and occasionally to Omilia offices or customer sites internationally) up to 30% of the time to support prospect meetings, POC delivery, and key account engagements.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Required:

  • Minimum 6 years of experience in a pre-sales solutions consulting, sales engineering, or technical advisory role within enterprise SaaS, CCaaS, conversational AI, or contact centre technology.
  • Demonstrated track record of owning the technical pre-sales motion for complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals — including discovery, solution design, POC delivery, and RFP response — with verifiable contribution to technical win rates.
  • Deep technical knowledge of contact centre architecture and integration patterns — including telephony (SIP, PSTN, WebRTC), CRM integrations (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft Dynamics), omnichannel platforms, and enterprise middleware.
  • Strong working knowledge of conversational AI concepts and technologies — NLU, dialogue management, ASR/TTS, intent classification, entity extraction, and voice biometrics — sufficient to engage credibly with customer platform architects and data science teams.
  • Proficiency in designing and delivering customised product demonstrations and POC environments that map directly to prospect business requirements and industry context.
  • Technical writing proficiency — able to produce clear, accurate, and commercially compelling responses to enterprise RFPs and RFIs, including security questionnaires, integration specifications, and compliance documentation.
  • Strong understanding of the enterprise IT landscape within regulated verticals — banking (OCC, FFIEC), healthcare (HIPAA, HL7/FHIR), insurance, and utilities — including security architecture, data governance requirements, and vendor evaluation processes.
  • Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills — able to engage a CTO or enterprise architect with technical depth while simultaneously communicating business value to a CFO or COO.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce CRM and standard pre-sales tooling (demo environments, solution configurators, proposal management platforms).

Nice to have:

  • Experience in a solutions consulting or SE role at a high-growth SaaS company scaling through Series C and beyond — familiarity with building pre-sales practice infrastructure (playbooks, demo environments, RFP libraries) in parallel with active deal execution.
  • Knowledge of US data privacy, AI governance, and voice data regulations relevant to enterprise deployments — CCPA, HIPAA, Illinois BIPA, and emerging federal AI frameworks.

  • Relevant certifications in cloud platforms, contact centre technologies, or AI/ML (e.g., AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Google Professional Cloud Architect, CCNA Collaboration).

Work at DaCodes! 🚀

At DaCodes, we build high-performing nearshore teams that partner with global companies to deliver cutting-edge technology solutions. We're driven by innovation, collaboration, and a passion for solving complex technical challenges across industries — and now we're looking for talented professionals to join one of our most exciting projects yet: a large-scale data integration modernization initiative for a leading higher-education institution in Australia.

We are searching for a Senior Informatica CDI Developer to join a strategic integration project for a higher-education client in Australia (~16,000 students/staff), delivered in partnership with a program management firm. The first phase covers five Canvas integrations over approximately 34 weeks, with MS Dynamics integrations to follow. The project is expected to kick off in January 2027.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain the change-detection engine for batch integrations.
  • Develop Banner extracts and conformance mappings.
  • Implement grade write-back processes between systems.
  • Design and maintain reconciliation controls to ensure data accuracy.
  • Support cutover activities and post-go-live hypercare.
  • Apply delta/change-detection patterns and build parameter-driven, reusable mappings.
  • Tune mapping performance through push-down optimization and bulk load strategies.

Requirements

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in Informatica, with 3+ years building CDI mappings and taskflows in production.
  • Experience with delta/change-detection patterns and parameter-driven mappings.

  • Experience with performance tuning (push-down optimization, bulk load) and reconciliation controls.

jobs.description:
Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) is responsible for developing, leading and executing the group-wide procurement, strategic sourcing and supplier management strategy across all subsidiaries, business units, operating entities and geographical markets within the organization.

The role provides strategic leadership over procurement governance, commercial negotiations, vendor relationships, cost optimization, third-party risk management, procurement operations and sourcing transformation. The Group CPO ensures procurement activities support the organization's financial performance, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, business continuity and strategic objectives.

Within an Insurance & Investments group, the role oversees procurement of technology, insurance operations, investment-related services, professional services, outsourcing, facilities, corporate services and other strategic goods and services.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Group Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement the group-wide procurement strategy aligned with corporate objectives, financial targets and business priorities.
  • Establish procurement policies, frameworks, standards and operating models across subsidiaries and business units.
  • Lead centralized, decentralized or hybrid procurement structures to optimize group-wide purchasing activities.
  • Drive procurement maturity, operational efficiency and strategic sourcing capability across the organization.
  • Advise executive leadership and the board on procurement strategy, commercial opportunities and supplier-related risks.

B. Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across major procurement categories, including IT, insurance operations, investment services, consulting, outsourcing, facilities and corporate services.
  • Develop category strategies, sourcing plans, supplier selection frameworks and procurement roadmaps.
  • Oversee competitive bidding, RFPs, RFQs, tendering, vendor evaluations and contract award processes.
  • Identify opportunities for group-wide procurement consolidation, economies of scale and supplier rationalization.
  • Drive strategic negotiations to secure commercial value, quality, service delivery and contractual protection.

C. Supplier & Vendor Management

  • Establish and oversee strategic supplier relationship management frameworks across the group.
  • Manage relationships with key suppliers, strategic partners, technology providers, outsourcing partners and service providers.
  • Develop supplier performance management frameworks, service-level agreements (SLAs), scorecards and review mechanisms.
  • Monitor supplier delivery, service quality, financial stability, contractual obligations and operational performance.
  • Lead supplier escalation, renegotiation, remediation and relationship improvement initiatives.

D. Cost Optimization & Financial Management

  • Drive procurement-led savings, cost optimization, cost avoidance and financial efficiency across group operations.
  • Develop procurement budgets, savings targets, spend forecasts and financial reporting frameworks.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize operating expenditure (OPEX), capital expenditure (CAPEX) and vendor spending.
  • Collaborate with Finance, business leaders and subsidiary management to validate procurement savings and benefits realization.
  • Monitor procurement spend, budget performance, financial controls and cost reduction initiatives.

E. Contract & Commercial Management

  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, strategic contract agreements, supplier terms and procurement-related commitments.
  • Establish group-wide contract management standards, renewal controls and commercial governance.
  • Ensure contracts reflect pricing, performance requirements, service levels, risk allocation, termination provisions and business continuity obligations.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Risk and Compliance teams on contract review, commercial risk and regulatory obligations.
  • Monitor contract lifecycle management, renewals, variations, disputes and contractual performance.

F. Procurement Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish procurement governance frameworks, delegated authority structures, approval processes and procurement controls.
  • Ensure procurement practices comply with regulatory requirements, internal policies, ethical standards and corporate governance.
  • Oversee supplier due diligence, procurement risk assessments, conflict-of-interest controls and supplier integrity checks.
  • Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and Legal teams to manage procurement-related risks.
  • Ensure procurement transparency, audit readiness, accountability and responsible purchasing practices.

G. Third-Party Risk & Outsourcing Management

  • Lead group-level oversight of third-party relationships, outsourced services and strategic vendor dependencies.
  • Ensure supplier risk assessment, due diligence, onboarding, monitoring and exit management processes are implemented.
  • Manage third-party operational, cybersecurity, data privacy, financial, reputational and business continuity risks.
  • Oversee critical supplier and outsourcing arrangements relevant to insurance and investment operations.
  • Ensure third-party governance aligns with the organization's risk management framework and applicable regulatory expectations.

H. Procurement Transformation & Digitalization

  • Drive procurement transformation initiatives to improve sourcing efficiency, automation, analytics and process standardization.
  • Implement or oversee procurement technology, e-procurement, spend analytics, contract management and supplier management platforms.
  • Leverage data analytics and technology to improve procurement visibility, forecasting, supplier performance and decision-making.
  • Lead process redesign, procurement operating model transformation and digital procurement adoption.
  • Promote continuous improvement, innovation and best practices across the group procurement function.

I. Executive Stakeholder & Business Partnership

  • Partner with Group CEO, COO, CFO, CIO, business unit leaders and subsidiary executives on procurement priorities.
  • Align procurement strategies with business growth, transformation, investment, operational and organizational priorities.
  • Provide executive-level procurement insights, recommendations, performance reports and strategic analysis.
  • Influence senior stakeholders on sourcing decisions, supplier strategy, commercial risk and cost optimization.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships to ensure procurement delivers business value.

J. Team Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Lead, develop and oversee group procurement, strategic sourcing, category management and vendor management teams.
  • Establish organizational structures, talent development plans, performance expectations and succession strategies.
  • Promote procurement excellence, ethical conduct, accountability, collaboration and commercial awareness.
  • Build procurement capability across subsidiaries, business units and regional operations.
  • Drive leadership development, performance management and continuous professional development.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Supply Chain Management, Procurement or Strategic Management preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, MCIPS or equivalent procurement qualifications are highly desirable.

Professional Experience

  • 12–18+ years of progressive procurement, sourcing, commercial or supply chain experience.
  • Significant experience in senior procurement leadership, preferably at Director, VP or C-suite level.
  • Proven experience leading group-wide, multi-entity, multinational or multi-business procurement functions.
  • Strong experience in strategic sourcing, category management, contract negotiation and supplier management.
  • Demonstrated track record of delivering measurable cost savings, procurement transformation and commercial value.
  • Experience managing procurement across complex organizations, regulated industries or financial services environments.
  • Experience in third-party risk management, outsourcing governance and supplier performance management.
  • Exposure to insurance, investment management, banking, financial services or other highly regulated industries is preferred.

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Group-wide procurement strategy and governance.
  • Strategic sourcing and category management.
  • Commercial negotiation and contract management.
  • Supplier relationship and vendor management.
  • Spend analytics and financial management.
  • Third-party risk and outsourcing oversight.
  • Procurement transformation and digitalization.
  • Regulatory compliance and corporate governance.

- Executive stakeholder management.

  • Organizational leadership and team development.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

KPI CategoryPerformance Indicators

Cost SavingsProcurement savings, cost avoidance and cost optimization achieved across the group.

Spend ManagementSpend under management, procurement spend visibility and strategic spend coverage.

Sourcing EffectivenessCompetitive sourcing rates, sourcing cycle time and sourcing strategy execution.

Supplier PerformanceSupplier SLA achievement, quality, delivery performance and supplier scorecard results.

Contract ManagementContract compliance, contract coverage, renewal management and negotiated commercial value.

Procurement CompliancePolicy compliance, approval adherence, audit findings and procurement control effectiveness.

Third-Party RiskSupplier risk assessment completion, critical supplier monitoring and risk remediation.

Operational EfficiencyProcurement cycle time, process efficiency and procurement service delivery.

TransformationProcurement technology adoption, automation and process improvement outcomes.

LeadershipProcurement team performance, capability development, stakeholder satisfaction and succession readiness.

Symmetrio is recruiting a Director of Product Development for a healthcare software company building AI-enabled tools for radiation oncology. This role will lead the clinical side of product development for software that supports physician consultations, treatment prescribing, on-treatment visits, and follow-up care.

You’ll work directly with radiation oncologists and their care teams to understand how they practice, identify where software can improve their workflow, and translate those findings into requirements. You’ll partner with product, design, and engineering from discovery through release, then work with early customers to verify that new features perform as intended in clinical practice. This is a hands-on director role with no direct reports.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead clinical discovery with U.S. radiation oncology practices through on-site observation, customer interviews, and feedback from live deployments. Identify recurring needs that should inform product priorities.
  • Translate clinical workflows into product requirements and acceptance criteria. Partner with the Product Owner, design, and engineering to review specifications and test prototypes before development.
  • Help design AI-assisted workflows that give clinicians clear opportunities to review, confirm, or override recommendations and preserve an audit trail.
  • Guide clinical validation through user acceptance testing, go-live, and early post-launch support. Document findings and provide clinical input on release readiness.
  • Partner with implementation teams on early deployments, including on-site workflow mapping and issue resolution. Document repeatable processes and train the implementation team as deployments mature.
  • Serve as the product escalation point for complex clinical questions from Sales, Customer Success, and Support. Use recurring issues to inform product improvements.
  • Contribute to clinical evidence gathering, regulatory documentation, and ongoing oversight of AI-enabled features.
  • Represent the company at industry meetings, advisory boards, and customer forums.

Requirements

What You’ll Bring

  • Clinical experience in U.S. radiation oncology as an oncology RN, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, medical dosimetrist with consult workflow experience, or in a comparable role.
  • Experience working closely with radiation oncologists and a practical understanding of how they conduct consultations, document findings, make treatment decisions, and handle related billing requirements.
  • Experience translating clinical needs into software requirements, evaluating prototypes, or validating clinical software in practice.
  • The ability to lead discussions with physicians and care teams and communicate their needs clearly to product, design, and engineering colleagues.
  • Experience using AI tools in your own work, such as synthesizing customer feedback or drafting and reviewing requirements.
  • Willingness to travel regularly within the U.S. and collaborate with distributed teams across time zones. Occasional international travel may be required.

The Role

We are looking for an IT Compliance Analyst to join Owlet's IT team and help execute our IT governance, risk, and compliance program. This is a hands-on role focused on doing the work: running control tests, gathering audit evidence, maintaining compliance documentation, and building the institutional knowledge that keeps Owlet audit-ready year-round. You will work under the direct guidance of the IT Director and alongside Internal Audit, Finance, and Legal as you grow into broader program ownership over time.

This is a strong fit for someone early in their GRC career who wants real SOX ITGC experience at a public company, without getting buried in a Big 4 engagement that keeps them three layers from the actual controls. You will see how the program runs from the inside and be given increasing ownership as you develop.

What You'll Do

SOX IT General Controls (ITGC)

  • Execute and document ITGC control testing across Owlet's key systems and platforms.
  • Collect, organize, and maintain control evidence in accordance with audit requirements.
  • Track control deficiencies and remediation items to closure under IT Director oversight.
  • Support SOX readiness activities and auditor walkthroughs, including preparing materials and responding to auditor requests.

Audit Support

  • Coordinate evidence collection and auditor access for internal audit, external financial audit, and SOC report engagements.
  • Maintain the audit evidence repository and ensure documentation is current, organized, and audit-ready throughout the year.
  • Serve as a reliable point of contact for auditor information requests, escalating to the IT Director as needed.

Policy and Documentation

  • Maintain Owlet's IT policy library: version control, review tracking, and attestation coordination.
  • Support annual policy review cycles by flagging outdated content and drafting proposed updates for IT Director review and approval.
  • Assist with communicating policy updates and awareness initiatives across the organization.

Compliance Risk and Controls

  • Maintain the IT compliance risk register: keeping entries current, tracking status, and flagging items that need IT Director attention.
  • Support IT change management processes to preserve audit trail integrity and separation of duties controls.
  • Assist with the IT component of third-party vendor compliance documentation as directed.

Requirements

  • 2-4 years of experience in IT compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or a GRC-adjacent role.
  • Foundational understanding of SOX ITGC concepts: access management, change management, computer operations, and logical security.
  • Experience executing or supporting ITGC control testing and evidence collection.
  • Strong written communication: you produce clear, well-organized documentation that holds up under audit scrutiny.
  • Detail-oriented and dependable: you track your own work, meet deadlines, and flag issues before they become problems.

Preferred

  • Experience in a regulated industry: medical devices, healthcare, financial services, or similar.
  • Exposure to SOC 1 or SOC 2 engagements (as a participant or evidence coordinator).
  • Familiarity with ERP environments from a controls perspective (NetSuite experience a plus).
  • Relevant certifications or coursework: CISA, CRISC, or audit-focused academic background.
  • Comfort working in a lean team where you build process as much as you follow it.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days, you will have a solid grasp of Owlet's current ITGC control inventory, know where the evidence lives, and be executing testing cycles with minimal ramp-up friction. By the end of year one, you are running audit coordination largely independently, the risk register is current without being prompted, and you have identified at least one area of process improvement you can own. The growth path from here leads to full program ownership as your experience and organizational context deepen.

Benefits

Owlet offers a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance:

  • Health & Wellness: Multiple medical plan options (PPO and High-Deductible with HSA), plus dental, vision, life, and disability coverage. Wellness resources include mental health support, EAP access, and fitness incentives.
  • Financial Benefits: A competitive 401(k) plan with company match, employee stock purchase program, and potential equity grants.
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous flexible PTO policy, including Flex Fridays, paid parental leave (up to 14 weeks), and remote/hybrid work options.

Owlet Baby Care, Inc. is the equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are excited to hear from candidates across the U.S., though we are not able to hire in Hawaii or Alaska at this time.

We’re growing and looking for more awesome people to join our merry band of misfits. We are looking for people who share our understanding that when it comes to our commitment to our customers: we mean business. Especially given that the consequences of getting payroll wrong can sometimes be dire.

If you are the kind of person who has always wanted to make a difference and be heard at work, Wagepoint will give you plenty of opportunity to do just that.

The Role at High Level:

We’re looking for a talented People Operations Coordinator who enjoys tackling hard problems and wants to create meaningful impact for small businesses across Canada. You'll keep People Operations running day to day, own onboarding from pre-boarding through a new hire's first 90 days, turn our people data into useful insight, and lead the automation of our People Ops workflows and reporting. You will report directly to our People Operations Manager & People Business Partner.

What You'll Be Expected To Own:

  • Create a great first impression for every new hire, from welcome emails and Day 1 schedules to equipment and system access with IT, our Wagemate program pairings, and 30/60/90-day check-ins.

  • Be the go-to resource for employee questions, translating policy and benefits details into plain language and managing benefits resources, FAQs, and updates.

  • Support performance review and compensation cycles with logistics, communications, reminders, and data cleanup, and keep People Ops policies and documentation current.

  • Process HRIS changes accurately and on time, complete our HR compliance calendar tasks, and maintain SOPs, templates, and regular documentation audits.

  • Maintain the dataset behind our workforce planning, build ARR per FTE and talent density reporting, and keep our people dashboards (headcount, hiring, turnover, engagement) accurate and current.

  • Administer our learning management system (LMS), track mandatory training completion, follow up on outstanding training, and coordinate new learning rollouts and the company training calendar.

  • Maintain our tools, knowledge base and systems, including employee data and documentation, with accuracy and confidentiality.

  • Own the automation of People Ops workflows and reporting with IT, starting with the tasks that repeat most and take the most time, and track the hours you save.

  • Compile, analyze, and spot patterns in the data and bring them to People Ops leadership so plans rest on facts.

  • Help managers show up for their teams during key People moments with timely and effective guides, reminders, and resources.

  • Pitch in on engagement programs, recognition initiatives, all-hands, and team events, and support recruiting coordination during peak hiring.

What You Bring To The Table:

  • 1–2 years of experience in HR, People Operations, HR analytics, or a related administrative role.

  • Experience with an HRIS and/or an Applicant Tracking System (ATS).

  • Comfort working across Google Workspace, Slack, and learning management systems.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills (e.g., Google Sheets) and comfort building simple reports and dashboards.

  • A data-minded approach: you're accurate, curious about patterns, and able to explain numbers in plain language.

  • Experience with, or keen interest in, workflow automation and AI tools, such as HRIS workflows, no-code automation, and AI assistants.

  • Strong organization and attention to detail, so nothing falls through the cracks.

  • Discretion with sensitive people information and a privacy-minded approach, including working with anonymized data.

  • Warm, clear communication that gives new hires and employees a great experience.

  • You're adaptable, proactive, and self-directed, and you take ownership.

Bonus points if:

  • You have post-secondary education in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • You've already built workflow automations or reports that saved your team real time.

  • You're familiar with PIPEDA and Canadian HR compliance requirements.

  • You've used HiBob or a similar HRIS.

  • You're bilingual in English and French.

What We Bring To The Table:

Impact: Roll up your sleeves and directly contribute to the growth and success of Wagepoint by shaping our workforce.

Culture: The opportunity to work with the world’s friendliest team, solving interesting problems together with an endless amount of laughter (We work hard, but we always have time for a bad joke or two).

Remote:The ability to work from home, forever! Wagepoint is a remote company, so you don’t have to worry about commuting to an office. Plus, more time with your pets is always a bonus!

Ready to embark on an exciting journey with us? Apply now and help us build the future of Wagepoint!

We are building an extraordinary company and looking for talented, energetic, and motivated people to join our team. You can learn more about our Company, Culture and Values here:


EverPro, a business within EverCommerce, provides software and solutions designed to help home and field service businesses run and grow their companies with greater efficiency and confidence. EverPro brings together purpose-built tools across key trades - including field service, remodelling and roofing, landscaping, and pest and lawn - so service professionals can manage operations, engage customers, and drive long-term growth.

Our solutions support the full lifecycle of running a service business, from scheduling and dispatching work, to estimating, invoicing, and payments, to customer communication, reputation management, and business insights. About the Role

We’re seeking a Product Manager to improve how dispatchers and office teams plan, schedule, and coordinate work through Service Fusion, EverPro’s field service management platform.

Your focus will include dispatching, scheduling, Service Agreements, and recurring service workflows. You’ll help teams turn customer commitments into scheduled work, respond to changing priorities, and keep technicians and customers informed throughout the day.

Working with Product leadership, you’ll own a focused roadmap and lead discovery, prioritization, delivery, and iteration for your product area. You’ll partner closely with Design and Engineering to simplify complex workflows, reduce manual coordination, and help service businesses deliver reliable customer experiences.

Core Responsibilities

  • Own and prioritize a roadmap for dispatching, scheduling, Service Agreements, and related office workflows.
  • Build a deep understanding of how dispatchers manage technician availability, recurring work, urgent requests, and schedule changes.
  • Improve the Service Agreement lifecycle, including agreement setup, recurring visit planning, scheduling, renewals, and coordination with invoicing and payments.
  • Partner with the Mobile product team to keep office and field workflows connected.
  • Lead discovery, usability testing, and early access feedback to validate solutions before broader release.

Nice to have:

The EverCommerce team is distributed globally, with teams in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Jordan, New Zealand, and Australia. With a widely distributed team, we are used to working remotely across different time zones. This role will be remote. Please note that you must be eligible to work without sponsorship to qualify for this position, and this role may require travel to our Corporate Headquarters in Denver, Colorado, or to other office locations around North America.

EverCommerce is an equal opportunity employer and we value diversity at our company. jobs.excerpt: About ALC A la Carte Solutions (ALC) is an Inc.  5000 firm.
jobs.description:
About ALC
A la Carte Solutions (ALC) is an Inc. 5000 firm. We provide outsourced finance, accounting and HR services to about 80 businesses across the US. Our brand promise is Wow Professionally, Care Personally, and it shapes how we treat clients and each other.

The Role
ALC built its own operating platform, ALC PACE. It has already replaced several third-party tools and is on its way to being the one system our team uses to run the firm. We’re looking for a senior, hands-on builder to own it.

You’ll architect, write, review and ship code every day. You’ll use Claude Code and similar AI tools heavily, and you’ll own the quality of what they produce. You’ll also lead the build of ALC’s first products for clients: a client portal, plus AI agents and automations for client workflows.

This isn’t a ticket-taking job. It’s for someone at manager-to-director level who still wants to build. You’ll sit with the people who use the platform, learn how the business works, and build what actually moves it forward. As the platform grows, you’ll set the standards, documentation and release process that let it scale, and eventually let a team build on it.

This is a fully remote role for candidates based in Latin America. You’ll work in your local time zone. You’ll also need the flexibility to join meetings and support colleagues in the US and other time zones when the work calls for it. All work is in English.

Our Stack
ALC PACE · GitHub · Railway · Neon (Postgres) · Claude Code · HubSpot (migrating into PACE) · third-party APIs

What You’ll Do: Wow Professionally

  • Own the architecture: Turn PACE into one connected system. Reporting, time review, billing, CRM, client operations and HR workflows should all share a single Postgres data model.
  • Build and ship every day: Own features end to end, from the first conversation with a stakeholder through build, deployment and support. Ship through a clean, repeatable release process.
  • Replace outside tools with PACE: Lead the move of our HubSpot CRM into PACE, redesigning the process rather than copying the old tool. Recommend which tools to replace next.
  • Turn spreadsheets into apps: Convert Excel models (capacity planning, direct margin, client profitability) into live features.
  • Build client-facing products: Help build the client portal. Design multi-tenant permissions that keep each client’s data secure and separate.
  • Build AI agents and automations: Design, build and evaluate agents and automations for internal and client workflows, including tool use, retrieval, prompt design and evaluation.
  • Own the quality of AI-written code: Review AI output like a draft from a talented junior engineer. Catch logic errors, security gaps and data-integrity problems before users see them.
  • Document everything: Write architecture, data model and runbook docs so the platform doesn’t depend on any one person’s knowledge.

How You’ll Show Up: Care Personally

  • Partner with stakeholders: Sit with leadership and department heads, ask good questions, and turn how they work into clear requirements. Push back respectfully when a request wouldn’t serve the bigger system.
  • Build with the business in mind: Know whether a feature saves time, improves margin or makes a client’s life easier, and prioritize accordingly.
  • Speak plainly: Explain technical tradeoffs and write updates that non-engineers can follow.
  • Drive adoption, not just delivery: Support the team through changes like the HubSpot migration so new tools actually get used.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 days: You’re set up locally, you know the architecture and data model, and you’ve shipped your first fixes to production.
  • 90 days: You’ve owned a meaningful feature end to end and written a prioritized plan for risk and technical debt.
  • 180 days: You’re the go-to owner for major parts of the platform. You’ve led a spreadsheet-to-app or HubSpot migration workstream, contributed to the client portal, and set standards others can build on.

Requirements

You Bring

  • A track record of real, shipped work. A degree isn’t required.
  • 7+ years building and shipping web applications, including owning production systems end to end.
  • Experience as a technical lead or architect: setting standards, reviewing code and owning a platform or product area.
  • Fluency in a modern web stack: JavaScript/TypeScript, React or similar, and Node or Python.
  • Strong SQL and data modeling, with Postgres preferred.
  • Hands-on integration work with REST APIs, webhooks and authentication flows.
  • Daily use of AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar), with examples of catching their mistakes.
  • Solid Git workflow and production deployment experience on a cloud platform.
  • Professional English, strong enough to lead stakeholder meetings and write documentation for non-technical colleagues.
  • Flexibility to work across time zones, including regular overlap with US-based colleagues.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building AI agents or LLM-powered workflows
  • Experience replacing SaaS products with custom software, or building internal tools or ERPs
  • Experience migrating HubSpot or other CRM data
  • Exposure to finance, accounting, HR or professional services operations
  • Experience building multi-tenant client portals
  • Experience with Railway, Neon or similar platforms

How You Think
You’re a systems thinker: before you build, you ask where the data comes from, where it goes and what else it touches. You can take a loosely defined problem, scope it and ship something useful. You move fast with AI tools without trusting them blindly.

Benefits

  • Pay: $5,000 – $6,500 USD per month ($60,000 – $78,000 USD per year), depending on experience
  • Full-time employment through our employer-of-record partner, including statutory benefits required in your country
  • Flexible PTO with no set maximum. If you take fewer than 10 days a year, we’ll nudge you to take more.
  • All ALC company holidays off
  • Fully remote, working in your local time zone
  • A chance to build a platform from the ground up at a growing Inc. 5000 firm
  • Direct work with ALC’s leadership team and a real say in the product

jobs.description:
Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Group Chief Procurement Officer (Group CPO) is responsible for developing, leading and executing the group-wide procurement, strategic sourcing and supplier management strategy across all subsidiaries, business units, operating entities and geographical markets within the organization.

The role provides strategic leadership over procurement governance, commercial negotiations, vendor relationships, cost optimization, third-party risk management, procurement operations and sourcing transformation. The Group CPO ensures procurement activities support the organization's financial performance, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, business continuity and strategic objectives.

Within an Insurance & Investments group, the role oversees procurement of technology, insurance operations, investment-related services, professional services, outsourcing, facilities, corporate services and other strategic goods and services.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Group Procurement Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and implement the group-wide procurement strategy aligned with corporate objectives, financial targets and business priorities.
  • Establish procurement policies, frameworks, standards and operating models across subsidiaries and business units.
  • Lead centralized, decentralized or hybrid procurement structures to optimize group-wide purchasing activities.
  • Drive procurement maturity, operational efficiency and strategic sourcing capability across the organization.
  • Advise executive leadership and the board on procurement strategy, commercial opportunities and supplier-related risks.

B. Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across major procurement categories, including IT, insurance operations, investment services, consulting, outsourcing, facilities and corporate services.
  • Develop category strategies, sourcing plans, supplier selection frameworks and procurement roadmaps.
  • Oversee competitive bidding, RFPs, RFQs, tendering, vendor evaluations and contract award processes.
  • Identify opportunities for group-wide procurement consolidation, economies of scale and supplier rationalization.
  • Drive strategic negotiations to secure commercial value, quality, service delivery and contractual protection.

C. Supplier & Vendor Management

  • Establish and oversee strategic supplier relationship management frameworks across the group.
  • Manage relationships with key suppliers, strategic partners, technology providers, outsourcing partners and service providers.
  • Develop supplier performance management frameworks, service-level agreements (SLAs), scorecards and review mechanisms.
  • Monitor supplier delivery, service quality, financial stability, contractual obligations and operational performance.
  • Lead supplier escalation, renegotiation, remediation and relationship improvement initiatives.

D. Cost Optimization & Financial Management

  • Drive procurement-led savings, cost optimization, cost avoidance and financial efficiency across group operations.
  • Develop procurement budgets, savings targets, spend forecasts and financial reporting frameworks.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize operating expenditure (OPEX), capital expenditure (CAPEX) and vendor spending.
  • Collaborate with Finance, business leaders and subsidiary management to validate procurement savings and benefits realization.
  • Monitor procurement spend, budget performance, financial controls and cost reduction initiatives.

E. Contract & Commercial Management

  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, strategic contract agreements, supplier terms and procurement-related commitments.
  • Establish group-wide contract management standards, renewal controls and commercial governance.
  • Ensure contracts reflect pricing, performance requirements, service levels, risk allocation, termination provisions and business continuity obligations.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Risk and Compliance teams on contract review, commercial risk and regulatory obligations.
  • Monitor contract lifecycle management, renewals, variations, disputes and contractual performance.

F. Procurement Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Establish procurement governance frameworks, delegated authority structures, approval processes and procurement controls.
  • Ensure procurement practices comply with regulatory requirements, internal policies, ethical standards and corporate governance.
  • Oversee supplier due diligence, procurement risk assessments, conflict-of-interest controls and supplier integrity checks.
  • Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit and Legal teams to manage procurement-related risks.
  • Ensure procurement transparency, audit readiness, accountability and responsible purchasing practices.

G. Third-Party Risk & Outsourcing Management

  • Lead group-level oversight of third-party relationships, outsourced services and strategic vendor dependencies.
  • Ensure supplier risk assessment, due diligence, onboarding, monitoring and exit management processes are implemented.
  • Manage third-party operational, cybersecurity, data privacy, financial, reputational and business continuity risks.
  • Oversee critical supplier and outsourcing arrangements relevant to insurance and investment operations.
  • Ensure third-party governance aligns with the organization's risk management framework and applicable regulatory expectations.

H. Procurement Transformation & Digitalization

  • Drive procurement transformation initiatives to improve sourcing efficiency, automation, analytics and process standardization.
  • Implement or oversee procurement technology, e-procurement, spend analytics, contract management and supplier management platforms.
  • Leverage data analytics and technology to improve procurement visibility, forecasting, supplier performance and decision-making.
  • Lead process redesign, procurement operating model transformation and digital procurement adoption.
  • Promote continuous improvement, innovation and best practices across the group procurement function.

I. Executive Stakeholder & Business Partnership

  • Partner with Group CEO, COO, CFO, CIO, business unit leaders and subsidiary executives on procurement priorities.
  • Align procurement strategies with business growth, transformation, investment, operational and organizational priorities.
  • Provide executive-level procurement insights, recommendations, performance reports and strategic analysis.
  • Influence senior stakeholders on sourcing decisions, supplier strategy, commercial risk and cost optimization.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships to ensure procurement delivers business value.

J. Team Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Lead, develop and oversee group procurement, strategic sourcing, category management and vendor management teams.
  • Establish organizational structures, talent development plans, performance expectations and succession strategies.
  • Promote procurement excellence, ethical conduct, accountability, collaboration and commercial awareness.
  • Build procurement capability across subsidiaries, business units and regional operations.
  • Drive leadership development, performance management and continuous professional development.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Supply Chain Management, Procurement or Strategic Management preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as CIPS, CPSM, MCIPS or equivalent procurement qualifications are highly desirable.

Professional Experience

  • 12–18+ years of progressive procurement, sourcing, commercial or supply chain experience.
  • Significant experience in senior procurement leadership, preferably at Director, VP or C-suite level.
  • Proven experience leading group-wide, multi-entity, multinational or multi-business procurement functions.
  • Strong experience in strategic sourcing, category management, contract negotiation and supplier management.
  • Demonstrated track record of delivering measurable cost savings, procurement transformation and commercial value.
  • Experience managing procurement across complex organizations, regulated industries or financial services environments.
  • Experience in third-party risk management, outsourcing governance and supplier performance management.
  • Exposure to insurance, investment management, banking, financial services or other highly regulated industries is preferred.

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Group-wide procurement strategy and governance.
  • Strategic sourcing and category management.
  • Commercial negotiation and contract management.
  • Supplier relationship and vendor management.
  • Spend analytics and financial management.
  • Third-party risk and outsourcing oversight.
  • Procurement transformation and digitalization.
  • Regulatory compliance and corporate governance.

- Executive stakeholder management.

  • Organizational leadership and team development.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

KPI CategoryPerformance Indicators

Cost SavingsProcurement savings, cost avoidance and cost optimization achieved across the group.

Spend ManagementSpend under management, procurement spend visibility and strategic spend coverage.

Sourcing EffectivenessCompetitive sourcing rates, sourcing cycle time and sourcing strategy execution.

Supplier PerformanceSupplier SLA achievement, quality, delivery performance and supplier scorecard results.

Contract ManagementContract compliance, contract coverage, renewal management and negotiated commercial value.

Procurement CompliancePolicy compliance, approval adherence, audit findings and procurement control effectiveness.

Third-Party RiskSupplier risk assessment completion, critical supplier monitoring and risk remediation.

Operational EfficiencyProcurement cycle time, process efficiency and procurement service delivery.

TransformationProcurement technology adoption, automation and process improvement outcomes.

LeadershipProcurement team performance, capability development, stakeholder satisfaction and succession readiness.

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are Spectro Cloud helps platform teams and cloud providers modernize and manage infrastructure for the AI era without adding more tools or operational complexity.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Spectro Cloud helps platform teams and cloud providers modernize and manage infrastructure for the AI era without adding more tools or operational complexity.
With PaletteAI, enterprises, public sector organizations, neoclouds and sovereign clouds can build, govern and operate full-stack environments across VMs, Kubernetes, edge, regulated and air-gapped locations, and AI infrastructure. PaletteAI Launchpads help teams start quickly with urgent outcomes such as VMware migration, token cost control or edge modernization, then scale into enterprise-wide lifecycle management, governance and fleet operations on the same platform.

About The Team

The Partner Enablement Manager builds the partner-specific content that gets partner sellers and engineers selling and delivering Spectro Cloud, including AI. This person speaks partner sales (margin, rebates, deal registration, co-sell, services attach) and writes accurate technical material, then uses AI to turn a partner request into a usable asset in days, not weeks. They also own the certification framework that sits underneath it.

What You’ll Do

Bespoke partner content (~35%)

  • Build partner-specific kits for priority partners and the three customer plays (AI, Edge, Modern Infrastructure): positioning, one-pagers, battlecards, talk tracks, discovery guides, demo flows, lab guides, and short e-learning. Start from approved core assets and tailor them to the partner's value proposition, customer use case, and sales motion. Use AI to draft fast, then get technical review from SEs and Product and messaging approval from Marketing before anything ships. Keep a versioned library by use case in Allbound. Build AI roleplays so partner reps rehearse conversations before they meet customers.

Partner field engagement and iteration (~20%)

  • Run working sessions with partner sales and SE teams, in person and virtual, including pilots such as the Arrow session. Join live partner engagements, capture the questions partners ask and where deals stall, and update kits within days. Translate between Product and partner sellers in both directions. Send gaps back to Product, Marketing, and Channel.

Certification framework (~25%)

  • Own the Sales and Tech tracks across Tier 1 (Associate), Tier 2 (Professional), and Tier 3 (Expert). Start Tier 2 specialist paths with Instinct Coder, then add paths such as VMware modernization, token cost control, and AI factories. Scope labs with the Technical team. Run Tier 3 case-study reviews and Delivery Readiness Assessments with Doug. Keep content current with the 24-month recertification cycle and the quarterly content audit. Manage the certification platform (Spectro U), including the Flockjay to Moodle move.

AI-powered program ops (~20%)

  • Automate certification tracking, tier reporting, and eligibility checks across the LMS, Allbound, and Salesforce. Own the rules for individual certification SPIFFs and the Launchpad, Ascent, and Orbital tiers, and hand payout administration to Channel Operations. Support partner program design once margin, rebate, pricing, and tier decisions are final. Report time saved and share what works with the wider Enablement team.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years in partner enablement, channel marketing, partner sales engineering, or channel sales in B2B tech.
  • Fluent in partner sales: deal registration, margin and rebates, MDF, co-sell, services attach, and tiering. Credible in a partner QBR.
  • Hands-on builder of technical content: decks, battlecards, lab guides, demo scripts, and e-learning that SEs and Product sign off on.
  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes, cloud, and virtualization, and of how AI is deployed and run (GPUs, inference, data center to edge).
  • Daily use of AI assistants and agents (for example Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot) to build content, analyze data, and automate work. Has built prompts, projects, or agents that other people use.
  • A repeatable method for checking AI-generated technical content against product docs and SMEs before it reaches a partner.
  • Curriculum and certification design, including assessments and labs.
  • Experience with an LMS (Moodle preferred, including SCORM, SSO, and badging).
  • Program management across many owners, comfortable with spreadsheets, dashboards, and tracking systems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Allbound, Salesforce, or another partner relationship management tool.
  • Partner economics and SPIFF design.
  • GTM work with GPU and OEM ecosystems (NVIDIA, AMD, Supermicro, Dell).
  • Public sector or federal partner exposure (VerteX, DDIL, air-gap).
  • Video, courseware, or e-course production.

This is a hands-on operating role. You will be in the data every day, finding where approvals drop or customers abandon, and fixing it with Product, Engineering, Finance and Risk.

Checkout and payment page optimization

Subscription and recurring billing

jobs.excerpt: About Sardina Systems Sardina Systems builds cloud infrastructure software based on OpenStack, Kubernetes, and Ceph for cloud operators, enterprises, and service providers across the globe.
jobs.description:
About Sardina Systems

Sardina Systems builds cloud infrastructure software based on OpenStack, Kubernetes, and Ceph for cloud operators, enterprises, and service providers across the globe. Behind our technology is a distributed team of builders creating reliable systems for our users.

Position summary

Build and operate a live kernel patching feed for AlmaLinux 10. You own the full technical chain, from CVE triage to signed, tested RPMs published in a public repository. This is a hands-on kernel engineering role, not a management or release-coordination position.

Core responsibilities

Patch engineering

  • Track AlmaLinux security advisories (ALSA) and upstream kernel CVEs.
  • Triage CVEs against the published scope: critical, remotely exploitable or actively exploited vulnerabilities.
  • Backport security fixes to the supported AlmaLinux 10 kernels, resolving conflicts across version differences.
  • Generate live patch modules with klp-build. Initially, publish individual CVE patches; evaluate cumulative/atomic replace strategies as the pipeline matures.
  • Identify CVEs that cannot be live patched (e.g. __init changes, data structure layout changes) and record them in the coverage-gap log.

Build and distribution pipeline

  • Reproduce AlmaLinux kernel builds exactly (same source, config and compiler), e.g. in mock with the AlmaLinux buildroot, so modules match the running kernel.
  • Maintain the automated pipeline: CVE scan, build plan, klp-build, RPM packaging, signing, test gate, createrepo_c publication.
  • Plan and execute the move of support to new AlmaLinux kernel releases as they ship.
  • Verify the exact client-side commands work on stock AlmaLinux 10 (dnf kpatch auto plus kpatch-patch-* packages).

Testing and release gate

  • Run the mandatory pre-publication gate on every patch:
  • load and unload on the target kernel in QEMU;

- run kernel livepatch selftests;

  • for high-severity CVEs: apply and revert under load on a FishOS test cluster with running VMs and Ceph I/O.
  • Document which tests were passed for each release.
  • A patch that passes the gate is cleared for publication. Do not publish a patch that has failed the gate.

Release and withdrawal

  • Publish approved patches with release notes listing the CVEs covered.
  • Publish the source for every released patch alongside its RPM.
  • If a published patch misbehaves: pull it from the repository, publish an advisory, and give users revert instructions.
  • Maintain the runbook and coverage-gap log.

Secure Boot

  • Manage the Sardina module-signing key and RPM signing key.
  • Document and verify mokutil key enrolment for AlmaLinux users.
  • Work with the Ops team to automate key enrolment on FishOS.

Required skills

  • Linux kernel development: strong C, with hands-on experience backporting kernel patches or debugging kernel modules. Screening will test this directly.
  • Live patching: practical experience with klp-build or kpatch, or demonstrated ability to learn them quickly from source.
  • RPM and the RHEL/AlmaLinux ecosystem: kernel packaging (RPM/SRPM), mock, dnf, createrepo_c and repository metadata.
  • Automation: Python or shell; building and maintaining CI-style pipelines.
  • Signing: GPG key management and RPM signing; kernel module signature verification and MOK enrolment.

- English: working proficiency.

Preferred skills

  • Spoken Russian and/or Mandarin, in addition to English. This is to work closely with Russian- and Mandarin-speaking team members.
  • QEMU-based VM validation or canary testing.
  • Upstream kernel contributions or involvement in the live patching community.
  • Koji or similar build orchestration systems.
  • Ceph I/O testing or storage-heavy workloads.

Key traits

  • Boundary awareness: Willing to say plainly "this CVE needs a reboot" and "this kernel is out of scope" rather than forcing a risky patch
  • Release discipline: Understands that a bad patch is the main reputational risk and will not skip the test gate under pressure
  • Self-directed: Comfortable owning an end-to-end pipeline with minimal supervision
  • Confidentiality: handles embargoed vulnerabilities and unreleased plans with discretion.

Working context

  • Scope: AlmaLinux 10 only, starting with one kernel version.
  • Infrastructure: runs separately from the existing Koji-based OpenStack build infrastructure, but follows the same automation approach.
  • Primary tooling: klp-build, kpatch/kpatch-dnf, mock, createrepo_c, GPG, systemd timers, QEMU and a FishOS test cluster.
  • Release authority: Routine patches are approved by the automated gate; no per-patch sign-off is required. A named release authority reviews weekly summaries, approves exceptions (e.g., a patch that cannot pass the full gate for a documented reason), and handles emergency withdrawals.
  • Backup: one Ops team member is cross-trained on the test gate, publication and withdrawal steps early in the project.

Success Criteria

First milestone

  • klp-build confirmed working on a real Alma 10 kernel
  • End-to-end pipeline producing a signed, tested patch for one CVE class on one kernel version
  • Test gate passed on at least two consecutive builds

- Coverage-gap log and runbook exist

Second milestone

  • Pipeline operating reliably with the test gate on every build
  • Secure Boot enrollment automated on FishOS
  • Sources and tooling published under the appropriate license
  • Runbook and coverage-gap log maintained and current

Working with us

You can work from anywhere in the Asia Pacific region with our remote work setup. We also provide mentoring sessions to support your continuous growth and technical development.

​​Looking for Philippines-based candidates

Job Role: Insurance Admin Assistant

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be engaged directly by the client as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: We operate within the financial services and personal insurance industry, helping individuals, families, and business owners protect their financial wellbeing against unexpected life events. Our focus is on making insurance more accessible, straightforward, and affordable through tailored coverage options and expert guidance.

We provide general advice on Life, TPD, Trauma and Income Protection cover. Clients come through mortgage brokers and an SMSF accounting partner. We place cover with 11 Australian retail insurers, and our licensee is Sustainable Life Solutions.

Role Overview: We are looking for an experienced life insurance Admin Assistant to work remotely from the Philippines. The role is the founder's right hand and starts in mid-to-late January 2027.

We serve about 620 clients and submit 25 to 35 applications a month. We run 20 to 30 client appointments a week. This role takes over the day-to-day processing, follow-up, and client servicing to help us focus on clients, broker partners, and growing the business

Key Responsibilities:

The priority is clearing outstanding underwriting requirements so applications get to completion. There are about 30 such pending cases today.

1. Suspense and new business management (priority)

  • Track every submitted application through to completion across 12 insurers.
  • Once an application is submitted, order any blood tests or medicals with the paramedical agency as soon as possible.
  • Follow up outstanding underwriting requirements with clients, doctors and insurers. These include medicals, blood tests, GP and specialist reports, financial evidence and signed forms.
  • Work with insurers' Business Development Managers (BDMs) to push stalled cases through, liaising directly with each insurer's new business and underwriting teams as needed.
  • Keep clients updated in plain English so applications don't stall.
  • Prepare and process implementation paperwork once cover is accepted.
  • Once the policy is issued, update the CRM with the policy details. These include the insurer, policy number, cover types and amounts, premium, commencement date, and any loadings or exclusions.
  • For replacement cover, such as moving clients from super-fund cover to a retail policy, make sure the old cover isn't cancelled until the new policy is in force.

2. Follow-up of quoted clients and lead management

  • Follow up clients via email or SMS who have been presented with insurance options but haven't proceeded.
  • Book them back in with John to complete the application, or confirm they don't wish to go ahead.
  • Close leads that won't proceed in the CRM, with the reason recorded.
  • Update the referring mortgage broker or partner on the outcome of every lead they sent.

3. Diary management

  • Manage John's calendar in Outlook, booking 20 to 30 client appointments a week.
  • Confirm appointments, send reminders and reschedule no-shows.
  • Protect blocks of time for strategy work and broker meetings.

4. CRM and record keeping

  • Keep client records, file notes and documents complete and up to date in the licensee's CRM (Sustainable Life Solutions).
  • Make sure every client file meets the licensee's compliance standards.
  • Manage client documents in SharePoint and keep filing consistent.

5. Renewals and client retention

  • Prioritize clients ahead of their annual policy anniversary based on pre-determined criteria.
  • Flag premium increases, failed payments and lapse notices to John early. Early action protects clients' cover and reduces the risk of commission clawbacks.

6. Client service and policy changes

  • Respond promptly to client admin requests. These include address and payment detail changes, beneficiary updates, policy documents and premium queries.
  • Lodge policy alterations with insurers and confirm the outcome with clients.
  • Refer any question about what cover a client should have to John. The assistant does not give advice.

7. Marketing support

  • Post updates to Shield Life's social media channels.
  • Keep broker partner contact lists current.

8. General admin

  • Triage John's inbox and draft routine replies.
  • Help track commission statements against submitted business.
  • Document processes as they are learned so the business can scale.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

  • 3+ years in insurance administration, ideally in life insurance: Relevant roles include new business, underwriting support, policy servicing or adviser support.
  • Fluent in the language of insurance: The candidate should be confident with terms like underwriting requirements, exclusions, loadings, premiums, policy anniversaries and lapses.
  • Strong follow-through: The candidate chases outstanding items without being asked and closes the loop with clients, insurers and John.
  • Great attitude and a willingness to learn: The candidate should be positive and coachable, take ownership of their work, and be comfortable learning new systems and processes.
  • Microsoft 365: Confident with Outlook (including calendar management), Word, Excel, Teams and SharePoint.
  • Excellent written and spoken English: The candidate must be clear and professional with Australian clients over email and phone.
  • Detail and organisation: The candidate can manage many open cases at once with nothing slipping through the cracks.
  • Discretion: The candidate handles sensitive personal, medical, and financial information confidentially.

Desirable skills

  • Australian life insurance experience: This could be within an Australian risk advice, financial planning, mortgage broking or SMSF practice.
  • Australian insurer platforms: Experience with retail insurer adviser portals and online application systems.
  • Adviser CRM systems: Experience with platforms such as Xplan, AdviserLogic or a licensee CRM.
  • Mailchimp: Experience building, scheduling and reporting on email campaigns.
  • Social media: Experience posting business updates on LinkedIn and Facebook, and using a scheduling tool.
  • Basic design tools such as Canva for newsletter and social graphics.
  • Australian privacy awareness: An understanding of Australian privacy obligations when handling client information.
  • Ambition to grow: An interest in growing into a senior admin or team lead role as Shield Life adds advisers in 2027.

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

This is a remote role that will be set up as an independent contractor engagement.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:
