  • Mentor senior engineers and raise the team's platform engineering practices.

What We're Looking For
  • 12–15 years of software engineering, with a substantial part of it spent building platforms: cloud, developer, container, or internal platforms, or as a software architect with deep platform knowledge.
  • Very strong Kubernetes: you have designed and run production workloads on it, and you understand networking, scheduling, security, multi-tenancy, and operators, not just deployments.
  • Very good AWS: EKS, IAM, VPC networking, private endpoints, Terraform or CDK. You have built and operated a cloud platform before.
  • Solid understanding of AI platform concepts: LLM gateways, agent runtimes (Bedrock AgentCore or comparable), MCP, RAG and retrieval, skills and tool registries, evals, and AI observability. You can explain how each piece fits and where the risks are.
  • Strong distributed systems, API design, and security fundamentals.
  • Comfortable in Python, enough to build reference implementations and review code.
  • Experience working inside large enterprises, preferably regulated ones (financial services, insurance, healthcare). You know the difference between a policy you can configure around and one that forces a redesign.

This role is fully remote. You can work from anywhere you are authorized to work in the United States, with up to 10% travel to customer sites.

Position Type: Full-Time, Fully Remote

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Medical Billing Specialist to manage day-to-day medical billing and claims processes for a healthcare practice.

This role requires strong hands-on experience with Medicare Part B (professional) billing for physician practices, clinics, or healthcare providers. The ideal candidate understands the complete provider-side billing cycle, including professional claims submission, payment posting, denial management, and accounts receivable follow-up.

You should have practical experience working with CMS-1500 / 837P claims, CPT and HCPCS coding, modifiers, and Medicare reimbursement processes. Experience in a payer call center or general insurance support role alone will not meet the requirements for this position.

The successful candidate will independently manage billing workflows, resolve claim issues, and keep the Finance team informed of billing progress and outstanding items.

What You'll Own

1. Claims Submission & Management

  • Prepare, review, and submit accurate Medicare Part B professional claims on behalf of physicians, clinics, or healthcare providers.
  • Work with CMS-1500 forms and 837P electronic professional claims.
  • Ensure claims meet Medicare and other applicable payer requirements.
  • Review coding and documentation for accuracy before submission.
  • Monitor claim statuses and resolve submission errors promptly.

2. Payment Posting & Reconciliation

  • Post insurance payments, adjustments, and denials accurately to patient accounts.
  • Review Explanation of Benefits (EOBs) and Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA) records.
  • Reconcile payments against expected reimbursements.
  • Identify and investigate payment discrepancies.

3. Denial Management

  • Investigate denied and rejected Medicare and other insurance claims to identify root causes.
  • Prepare and submit corrected claims or appeals within required deadlines.
  • Address coding, documentation, and modifier-related issues.
  • Track recurring denial patterns and follow up to ensure resolution.

4. Accounts Receivable & Follow-Up

  • Monitor outstanding balances and follow up on unpaid or pending claims.
  • Contact Medicare and other insurance carriers to resolve payment delays and billing discrepancies.
  • Track aging accounts and prioritize outstanding claims.
  • Escalate unresolved issues when necessary.

5. Patient & Payer Communication

  • Respond to billing-related inquiries from patients and insurance representatives.
  • Communicate professionally with insurance carriers to resolve claim discrepancies and payment concerns.
  • Keep the Finance team updated on billing progress, outstanding items, and potential blockers.

6. Accuracy & Compliance

  • Maintain accurate billing records and supporting documentation.
  • Follow applicable healthcare billing regulations, Medicare guidelines, payer requirements, and internal Finance procedures.
  • Handle patient and payer information with strict confidentiality.

Requirements

  • 4–5 years of hands-on medical billing experience working directly for a physician practice, clinic, medical office, or healthcare provider.
  • Proven Medicare Part B billing experience is mandatory. Candidates must have worked with professional claims submitted on behalf of healthcare providers.
  • Practical experience with CMS-1500 forms and/or 837P professional claims.
  • Strong understanding of CPT and HCPCS coding, including the use of modifiers.
  • Working knowledge of Medicare billing and reimbursement processes.
  • Experience managing the provider-side billing cycle, including claims submission, payment posting, denial management, and AR follow-up.
  • Familiarity with medical billing or practice management systems such as eClinicalWorks (eCW), Kareo, AdvancedMD, athenaOne, or NextGen. Experience with comparable systems is also acceptable.
  • Familiarity with EOBs, ERAs, payment reconciliation, and insurance verification.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify and resolve billing discrepancies.
  • Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage daily billing tasks in a remote environment.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You have substantial hands-on experience handling Medicare Part B billing for physician practices or healthcare providers.
  • You understand the difference between professional/provider billing and payer-side insurance support.
  • You take ownership of billing tasks and follow through without constant supervision.
  • You can independently investigate claim denials, resolve discrepancies, and follow up on outstanding payments.
  • You are organized and consistent when handling repetitive, detail-oriented work.
  • You communicate clearly with the Finance team and external insurance representatives.
  • You understand the importance of accuracy, confidentiality, and timely follow-up in medical billing.

What Success Looks Like

  • Medicare Part B and other professional claims are submitted accurately and within required deadlines.
  • Payments are posted and reconciled consistently.
  • Denials are investigated and resolved promptly.
  • Outstanding AR balances receive timely follow-up.
  • Billing discrepancies are identified and addressed before they cause delays.
  • The Finance team has clear visibility into billing progress and outstanding issues.

ROLE: Yardi Systems Administrator

Salary: $3,500 USD/Monthly

POSITION SUMMARY:

We are seeking a highly skilled Yardi Systems Administrator to serve as the sole internal owner, technical expert, and platform strategist for our Yardi ecosystem. Our firm primarily invests in commercial retail real estate, meaning our operations require a deep understanding of complex retail leasing structures, intricate CAM reconciliations, and variable sales tracking.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between our technology stack and our business operations. You will be responsible for system configuration, user permissions, database health, custom reporting, and onboarding new retail assets. The ideal candidate doesn't just know how to configure Yardi—they understand the underlying financial and operational mechanics of commercial retail real estate.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • System Administration & Optimization
    • Serve as the primary point of contact and subject matter expert (SME) for all things related to Yardi Voyager (Commercial/Retail module) and integrated applications (e.g., CommercialCafe, Yardi Advanced Budgeting & Forecasting).
    • Manage user provisioning, custom security roles, workflow approvals, and system menus to ensure data security and compliance.
    • Lead the technical onboarding, data migration, and setup of newly acquired commercial retail assets into the Yardi database.
    • Monitor, test, and implement Yardi system updates, plug-ins, and new module rollouts, ensuring zero disruption to daily business operations.
  • Retail Operations & Financial Support
    • Support the property management and accounting teams with complex, retail-specific configurations, including Common Area Maintenance (CAM) setups, tax/insurance reconciliations, and recovery configurations.
    • Oversee the technical setup and execution of Percentage Rent parameters, gross sales tracking, and variable retail leasing structures.
    • Troubleshoot system errors related to retail lease administration, tenant billings, and recurring charge schedules.
  • Reporting & Business Intelligence
    • Design, develop, and maintain custom reports and dashboards using Yardi Spreadsheet Reporting (YSR), Yardi Correspondence, or SQL/SSRS to support executive decision-making.
    • Collaborate with asset management and finance teams to optimize data flow, automate manual workarounds, and ensure data integrity across all portfolios.

Requirements

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Finance, Real Estate, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
  • Yardi Expertise: Minimum of 3–5 years of hands-on administration experience specifically within Yardi Voyager Commercial/Retail. (Applications with purely residential or multifamily experience will not be considered).
  • Industry Knowledge: Solid understanding of commercial real estate accounting principles, commercial lease logic, and retail recovery mechanics (CAM, recurring charges, overage rent).
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency with Yardi database structures, database mapping, and writing custom reports (YSR, Yardi Script, or basic SQL query writing).
  • Preferred/Nice-to-Have:
    • Experience with Yardi Advanced Budgeting & Forecasting (ABF).
    • Experience implementing or managing CommercialCafe or tenant portals.
    • Prior experience working at a commercial real estate investment, asset management, or development firm.
  • Soft Skills:
    • Strong analytical troubleshooting skills—someone who loves solving complex data puzzles.
    • Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical jargon into clear business insights for non-technical team members.
    • Self-motivated and comfortable acting as the sole, go-to Yardi expert in the organization.

WORKING REQUIREMENTS

  • Fully remote
  • Fluent in English
  • Will work 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM US Eastern Time (EST)

jobs.description:
Join ShopMy - Powering the Future of Digital Marketing

ShopMy is transforming e-commerce by building the infrastructure for human-led curation at scale. We help brands run performance-driven creator programs while enabling top creators to monetize their influence and partner directly with the brands they love—driving discovery through trusted tastemakers and authentic recommendations.

ShopMy recently became a unicorn, raising at a $1.5B valuation with backing from Bessemer Venture Partners, Avenir Growth Capital, and Bain Capital Ventures.

At ShopMy, you're building the future of human-led commerce for the world's best brands, tastemakers, and shoppers. You move fast and see immediate impact in your work, alongside accomplished teammates who are driven by helping find the world's best things. If you’re excited to help shape the future of curated commerce at the intersection of technology, culture, and taste, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Director of Engineering building ShopMy's agent orchestration platform: the system our AI agents are built, run, managed, and improved on. Your job is the platform itself: the trigger layer that routes every inbound event from Slack, Linear, GitHub, and the ShopMy product; durable multi-step workflows; human-in-the-loop approvals; agent memory; evals; cost attribution; and the console it's all managed through. You'll partner closely with the agent managers who design and run the agents themselves. It's a small team with broad ownership, and the design challenge is keeping it a true platform - model-agnostic, with diverse triggers, composable workflows, and abstractions that make the next agent cheap to launch instead of a one-off build.

Your Impact to the Role

  • Design and evolve the orchestration core: a declarative trigger system spanning Slack, Linear, cron, and HTTP; durable workflows; and agent runs that can suspend and resume around human approval
  • Find the abstractions that keep the platform general, so the next agent or workflow composes existing machinery instead of forking a new code path
  • Build the tool layer that gives agents their capabilities: Slack, Linear, GitHub, Notion, MCP, and a dynamic tool registry
  • Build the management console agent managers use to create, evaluate, and improve agents (React)
  • Make agent behavior legible: run tracing, evals and judges, feedback loops, and per-run cost attribution
  • Design and implement APIs in TypeScript and NestJS backed by Postgres
  • Deploy and operate the platform on AWS (ECS, ALB, CloudFormation, CloudWatch)

You Are Energized By

  • Platform engineering with your users in the building: agent managers build on what you ship, and feedback arrives in hours, not quarters
  • Working where the patterns aren't established yet: durable execution, human-in-the-loop, memory, and evals for nondeterministic systems are problems you'll help define
  • Finding the abstraction that turns a special case into a capability
  • Solving complex technical challenges with clean, efficient, and scalable code

What We're Looking For

  • Strong proficiency in TypeScript, Node.js, and relational databases
  • Experience building systems other engineers build on: internal platforms, frameworks, orchestration or developer tooling, and the API design instincts that come with it
  • Enough hands-on time with LLMs to be comfortable building an agent yourself: tool calling, context and memory, and evaluating nondeterministic behavior
  • Experience building interfaces that make complex systems easy to understand and manage
  • Experience deploying and operating production services on AWS: containers, ECS, ALB, and monitoring with CloudWatch or similar
  • AI-assisted development (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) as a core part of how you work
  • Keen attention to detail in code structure and style
  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience

Bonus Points

  • You've built on or operated durable-execution or workflow engines (Temporal or similar), or rolled your own
  • You've shipped agent systems, built with agent frameworks (LangGraph, the Claude Agent SDK, or similar), written MCP servers, or built eval harnesses
  • Experience working in high-growth startups or fast-paced product environments
  • Enjoy mentoring and helping shape engineering best practices and team culture

ShopMy is flexible pending candidate's experience and how our business needs evolve throughout the search. Every employee of ShopMy receives equity on top of cash compensation!

jobs.title: GTM Engineer (m/w/d) – Sales-Automation, Daten & KI | Werkstudent:in / Teilzeit
jobs.excerpt: Was passiert eigentlich mit uns Menschen, wenn Maschinen immer smarter werden?
jobs.description:
Was passiert eigentlich mit uns Menschen, wenn Maschinen immer smarter werden? Diese Frage hat unseren Gründer dazu gebracht, das Institut für Zukunftsbildung (IZB) ins Leben zu rufen.

Mit unserer AZAV-zertifizierten Weiterbildung „KI Leader“ begleiten wir Beschäftigte, Arbeitsuchende und Geschäftsführer:innen dabei, KI für sich zu nutzen, statt sie zu fürchten. Dabei gilt eine klare Arbeitsteilung: Maschinen verarbeiten Daten, erkennen Muster und liefern Prognosen. Fragen, fühlen, führen bleibt menschlich.

So arbeitet auch unser Vertrieb. Unser Vertriebsteam führt die Gespräche. Du baust die Maschine dahinter: Datenflüsse, Automationen und KI-Workflows, die ihnen die richtigen Impulse zur richtigen Zeit liefern, mit dem richtigen Kontext.

Wer wir sind, erzählt unser Gründer in zwei Minuten: youtube.com/shorts/9KnSv1V_vzY

Worum es wirklich geht: Du denkst Vertrieb von Ende zu Ende, vom ersten Datensatz bis zu der Person, die tatsächlich in unserer Weiterbildung startet.

Deine ersten Projekte

  1. Leadgenerierung automatisieren: Du baust ein System, das laufend neue passende Unternehmen findet und vorqualifiziert, anhand von Signalen, die von außen erkennbar sind, zum Beispiel Unternehmensgröße, Wachstum oder offene Stellen. Dafür nutzt du aktuelle KI-Modelle und Datenquellen, damit unsere Opener jeden Tag mit den vielversprechendsten Kontakten starten.

  2. Datenqualität im CRM verbessern: Wo Unternehmensdaten fehlen oder veraltet sind, baust du einen Recherche-Workflow, der öffentlich verfügbare Unternehmensinformationen automatisiert prüft und aktualisiert, zum Beispiel von Firmenwebsites und aus öffentlichen Registern. Datenschutz denkst du dabei von Anfang an mit.

  3. Die Strecke für Arbeitsuchende automatisieren: Interessent:innen aus unseren Kampagnen sollen zur richtigen Zeit die richtigen Infos bekommen und den Weg bis zum Bildungsgutschein schaffen.

Danach gehört dir

  • Daten erschließen und pflegen: Workflows, die Daten aus Web-Quellen und APIs zusammenführen, prüfen und aktuell halten, mit eigenem Code und den passenden Tools.

  • Close weiterentwickeln: Pipelines, Smart Views und Workflows, damit unser Team weniger klickt und mehr im Kontakt ist.

  • KI-Assistenten bauen: Mit Langdock entstehen Helfer für Recherche, Gesprächsvorbereitung und Call-Zusammenfassungen.

  • Systeme verbinden: Über APIs, Webhooks und eigene Skripte fließen die Daten sauber zwischen unseren Tools.

Uns ist wichtiger, dass du die Technik beherrschst, als welche Tools du schon kennst. Tools lernst du schnell, wenn das Fundament steht.

Das bringst du mit

  • Code: Du programmierst, idealerweise in Python oder JavaScript, und arbeitest sicher mit APIs, Webhooks und JSON.

  • Eine Automation, die wirklich läuft: gebaut im Job, im Studium oder in einem eigenen Projekt. Genau die zeigst du uns in deiner Bewerbung.

  • Gespür für Zahlen: Du denkst in Conversion Rates und willst wissen, was am Ende herauskommt.

  • Sprache: Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau und gutes Englisch. Als Werkstudent:in bist du an einer Hochschule eingeschrieben.

Ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Erfahrung mit CRM-Systemen wie Close oder KI-Plattformen wie Langdock

  • Automatisierte Datenerfassung aus Web-Quellen und APIs, zum Beispiel mit eigenem Python-Code

  • Erfahrung als GTM Engineer, in RevOps, Growth oder Sales Ops

  • Wissen, was DSGVO und UWG im Vertrieb erlauben und was nicht

Benefits

  • Vergütung mit Upside: Fester Stundensatz plus Erfolgsbeteiligung für jede Person, die am Ende tatsächlich in unserer Weiterbildung startet. Nicht alles davon liegt in deiner Hand, aber genug, dass sich End-to-End-Denken für dich lohnt.

  • Steile Lernkurve: Unsere Vertriebsleitung arbeitet dich persönlich ein, und ihr arbeitet eng zusammen. Dabei lernst du Outbound auf dem neuesten Stand, von der Datenbasis bis zum Gespräch, das zum Abschluss führt.

  • Echte Gestaltungsfreiheit: Du baust unseren GTM-Stack maßgeblich mit auf und triffst echte Entscheidungen, mit kurzen Wegen bis in die Geschäftsführung.

  • Flexibel und remote: 100 % remote mit freier Zeiteinteilung. Ob Werkstudent:in, Teilzeit oder Minijob, finden wir gemeinsam heraus.

  • Perspektive mit Sinn: Die Weiterbildungsstarts für 2027 sind bereits geplant, und jede Automation, die du baust, hilft mehr Menschen, ganzheitliche KI-Kompetenz aufzubauen.

Statt eines Anschreibens freuen wir uns über ein Kurzvideo (max. 3 Minuten) oder einen Screenshot mit ein paar Sätzen dazu: Zeig uns einen Workflow, eine Integration oder ein Skript, auf das du stolz bist, und erklär kurz, welches Problem es löst. Schick uns einfach den Link.

So geht es danach weiter: Kurzes Kennenlernen per Video, dann ein Mini-Case aus unserem Vertriebsalltag, den du vorab bekommst und im Case-Gespräch (45 Minuten) vorstellst. Danach entscheiden wir.

Werde Teil des IZB und hilf uns, Menschen und Unternehmen in Deutschland fit für die Zukunft mit KI zu machen.

Wenn Sie leidenschaftlich daran interessiert sind, die Investmentwelt durch das Management und die Unterstützung von innovativen Venture-Fondsmanagern voranzubringen, dann könnte Allocator One der richtige Ort für Sie sein. Werden Sie Teil unseres Teams als Fonds- und Bilanzbuchhalter/in und spielen Sie eine zentrale Rolle beim Wachstum von Allocator One, indem Sie hohe Standards und effektive Abläufe gestalten und sicherstellen.

Als Mitglied unseres Kernteams werden Sie eng mit unseren Gründern, wichtigen Stakeholdern und anderen Experten zusammenarbeiten. Sie haben die Möglichkeit, vom kollektiven Wissen und der Expertise des Teams zu lernen und dazu beizutragen sowie an allen Aspekten der Wertschöpfungskette von Allocator One teilzunehmen. Die Position berichtet direkt an einen der Gründungspartner.

Hinweis: Der Hauptsitz von Allocator One befindet sich in Wien; unterstützen aber auch reine Home-Office Anstellungsverhältnisse.

Aufgaben

Allgemeine Verantwortlichkeiten:

  • Laufende Buchhaltung von offenen und geschlossenen Fonds, Führung der Anlagebücher und der Sachkonten, Durchführung der Kreditorenbuchhaltung und Stammdatenpflege
  • Übernahme, Auswertung und Kontrolle der Buchhaltungsdaten der Fondsmanager
  • Erstellung von Quartals- und Jahresabschlüssen nach UGB und IFRS
  • Prüfung von Transaktionsdokumenten und und Erstellung von Transaktions-Übersichtsblättern
  • Eigenständige Klärung von Differenzen und ad hoc Thematiken
  • Ansprechpartner/in für externe Prüfer und Berater
  • Fachliche/r Ansprechpartner/in in Projekten

Qualifikation

Ihre Fähigkeiten und Qualifikationen:

  • Ausgezeichnete Englischkenntnisse sind feste Vorraussetzung
  • Ausbildung als Bilanzbuchhalter/in, Steuerfachangestellte/r oder vergleichbarer Ausbildungshintergrund bzw. abgeschlossenes betriebswirtschaftliches Studium
  • Relevante Erfahrung in der Fonds- und Bilanzbuchhaltung, idealerweise im Bereich AIFMs
  • Fundierte buchhalterische sowie steuerliche Kenntnisse sind zwingend erforderlich
  • Abschlusssicher nach UGB
  • Mehrjährige Branchenerfahrung
  • BMD-Kenntnisse sind von Vorteil
  • Gute Kenntnisse der MS-Office-Programme (Word & Excel)
  • Teamfähigkeit und selbständiger Arbeitsstil

Benefits

Sozialleistungen, darunter:

  • Wettbewerbsfähiges Grundgehalt
  • Potenzial für Boni und Beteiligungen
  • Unternehmenskultur ohne Arroganz
  • Lernen und Wachsen mit erfahrenen Kollegen, die ihr Wissen gerne teilen
  • Mobiles und flexibles Arbeiten mit Vertrauensarbeitszeit
  • Moderne Arbeitswelten mit erstklassiger IT-Ausstattung
  • Vergünstigtes JobRad-Leasing
  • Strukturierte Einarbeitung, feste Ansprechpartner/innen, Feedbackgespräche und individuelle Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten durch interne und externe Seminarangebote

Über Allocator One

Bei Allocator One betreiben wir ein einzigartiges Fondsmodell, das darauf ausgelegt ist, in die vielversprechendsten Erst-Fondsmanager weltweit zu investieren und gleichzeitig die Gebühren zu optimieren. Angesichts der äußerst günstigen Aussichten für die Fondsjahrgänge 2023/2024 hat unser Team seine Bemühungen verstärkt, diese einzigartige Gelegenheit zu nutzen. Wir sind stolz darauf, der bevorzugte Ankerinvestor für außergewöhnliche Erst-Fondsmanager zu sein und ihnen unvergleichlichen Zugang, Expertise und operative Unterstützung zu bieten.

Unser Fokus auf Erst-Fondsmanager

Der Fokus von Allocator One auf Erst-Fondsmanager basiert auf einer einfachen, aber überzeugenden Tatsache: Historisch gesehen haben Spitzenfonds mit einem Vermögen von unter 50 Millionen Dollar, die von aufstrebenden Managern geführt werden, über einen Zeitraum von 10 Jahren Renditen erzielt, die mehr als dreimal so hoch sind wie die ihrer größeren Pendants. Darüber hinaus werden die Fondsjahrgänge 2023/2024 in unserem Portfolio voraussichtlich einen zusätzlichen Renditeanstieg verzeichnen. Venture-Capital-Fonds, die während wirtschaftlicher Rezessionen aufgelegt werden, haben durchweg Renditen erzielt, die 15%-30% höher sind als die der Jahre zuvor.

Optimierung von Gebühren und Aufbau von Partnerschaften

Wir glauben daran, Gebühren zu optimieren und gleichzeitig Partnerschaften mit Erst-Fondsmanagern von Anfang an zu pflegen. Unser Ziel ist es, die Investitionsbedingungen zu verbessern, indem wir aktiv zum Erfolg dieser Fonds beitragen. Allocator One hat sich dank unseres umfangreichen internationalen Investorennetzwerks bereits als globale Marke im Bereich der aufstrebenden Manager etabliert. In den ersten zwei Monaten seit unserem Start haben wir über 300 Bewerbungen erhalten, ein Beweis für unser Engagement zur Unterstützung aufstrebender Talente. Unser Team geht über traditionelle Investitionen hinaus; wir bieten an, als "Co-Builder" zu agieren und aufstrebende Manager in unser einzigartiges Allocator One-Programm zu integrieren, das oft als "Y Combinator für Kapitalallokatoren" bezeichnet wird. Wir bieten wesentliche Unterstützung in Bereichen wie Regulierung, Administration und Struktur.

Unsere Gründungspartner

Unsere Gründer bringen umfassende Erfahrung und Expertise zu Allocator One:

  • Felix Staeritz: Als Gründer des führenden Corporate Venture Builders FoundersLane verfügt Felix über eine beeindruckende Erfolgsbilanz im Aufbau und Verkauf erfolgreicher Unternehmen. Er ist ein aktiver VC/PE-Investor und sitzt in den Vorständen und Beiräten renommierter Organisationen wie dem Weltwirtschaftsforum (WEF), Fraunhofer und verschiedenen öffentlichen und privaten Unternehmen.
  • Michael Ströck: Michael ist ein erfahrener Unternehmer mit mehreren erfolgreichen Exits. Er ist Absolvent des Y Combinator und hat den Übergang von der CTO-Rolle zu einem erfolgreichen Investor geschafft. Michael hat eine Schlüsselrolle bei der Etablierung von drei VC-Fonds gespielt und ist Teil eines Familienunternehmens, das sich nun in der dritten Generation befindet.

Bewerbungsprozess

  1. Erstgespräch: Dieses erste Gespräch per Videoanruf mit einem Teammitglied bietet Ihnen die Möglichkeit, über Ihren Hintergrund und Ihre Erfahrungen zu sprechen und sicherzustellen, dass Sie die Mindestqualifikationen für die Rolle erfüllen und die Stelle Ihren Erwartungen entspricht.
  2. Interview mit den Gründungspartnern: Wenn Sie ein starker Kandidat sind, werden Sie zu einem Interview mit unseren Gründungspartnern eingeladen. Dies bietet Ihnen die Möglichkeit, mehr über die Strategie und Kultur des Unternehmens zu erfahren und den Partnern, Sie besser kennenzulernen.
  3. Case Study und/oder Assessment während eines Vor-Ort-Arbeitstages: Um sich noch besser kennenzulernen, laden wir Sie zu einem Arbeitstag in unser Büro in Wien ein. Zur Beurteilung Ihrer Fähigkeiten und Kenntnisse bitten wir Sie möglicherweise, eine Fallstudie oder ein Assessment zu absolvieren.
  4. Finales Interview: Nach dem finalen Interview wird das Team alle Kandidaten bewerten und eine Entscheidung treffen, wem das Angebot unterbreitet wird. Der Einstellungsprozess kann mehrere Wochen dauern, bitte haben Sie Geduld, während wir alle Bewerbungen überprüfen und eine Entscheidung treffen. Wenn Sie nicht für die Rolle ausgewählt werden, werden wir Sie so schnell wie möglich benachrichtigen.

Klingt interessant? Dann freuen wir uns auf Ihre Bewerbung!

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.excerpt: Role type: 1099 independent contractor, full time Location: Fully remote, LATAM About First Principles First Principles is a product consultancy founded by startup and enterprise product leaders.
locationRestrictions: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
jobs.description:
Role type: 1099 independent contractor, full time
Location: Fully remote, LATAM

About First Principles

First Principles is a product consultancy founded by startup and enterprise product leaders. Our focus is AI-first product management training. We help enterprise product and technology teams put AI to work in the jobs they already do, responsibly and productively. Almost every large company is trying to solve this problem right now.

Our programs are customizable, not custom. Clients choose from a catalog of practitioner-led classes across AI foundations, AI-first product management, and building AI products. We shape the program around their budget, goals, timeline, approved tools, and governance rules. A program can be a few focused sessions or a full 12 to 16 week certification. It can run virtually, on-site, or as a mix of both, for cohorts ranging from dozens of people to a couple hundred.

So far we have run three cohorts for Elsevier Health and a product and design focused program for another enterprise client. We also just launched a hybrid program with a national healthcare company. Healthcare is where we started, not where we plan to stop.

The Role

We are looking for a hunter who will open doors with enterprise product and technology leaders and turn those conversations into signed programs.

Until now, our deals have come almost entirely from relationships and referrals. That has worked, but it does not scale. Your job is to build a repeatable way of finding, starting, and closing new enterprise training engagements.

You own every deal from the first call to the signed contract, and everything in between. You create most of your own pipeline. You will work closely with our marketing lead, but you do not wait for inbound. Your time goes to prospects.

What our deals look like:

  • Size. Deals so far have ranged from $50,000 to $250,000.
  • Buying group. Usually a product leader who champions the program, a budget owner above them, and procurement. The champion can be anyone from an executive director or VP of product up to a chief product or chief AI officer.
  • Cycle length. Cycles are measured in months. Our most recent client went from first call to signed contract in about five months, and its first session ran two weeks after signing. You need the patience to run a long cycle and the urgency to keep it moving.

We sell to large enterprises, and they expect polish as a baseline. As a small, boutique firm, we have to be noticeably better than that baseline in every email, call, and proposal to stand out.

You will have a monthly budget for tools, travel, events, and materials, and you decide how to use it. This is not a role where someone hands you a plan. You tell us what success looks like, how you will get there, and then you get it done.

Responsibilities

Build pipeline. Research and prioritize target accounts and buyers. Reach out through email, LinkedIn, and phone. Write every message for the specific person receiving it. We are not looking for templates with a name swapped in.

Own the full cycle. Run every deal from first call to signed contract, and everything in between.

  • Scoping and proposals. Every program is shaped to the client. You lead scoping: cohort size, classes, number of sessions, delivery format, assignments, and certification. Experienced members of our team can join calls as subject matter experts and review proposals with you before they go out.
  • Closing. Manage pricing, phased payment terms, NDAs, contracts, and procurement. Keep a clear, honest forecast.
  • Handoff and growth. Hand signed clients to our delivery team with everything they need to launch. Then stay close to the account, because clients often come back for more cohorts. One of our clients is already on its third.

Know the space. Build and keep current your understanding of three things:

  • how product teams work
  • how AI is changing their work
  • where enterprises are getting stuck on AI adoption

Our team will help you get up to speed.

Show up in person. When there is a US event, conference, or client meeting where our buyers will be, we want you there.

Keep the record. Log activity and deal notes in our CRM as you go, so anyone on the team can pick up a thread if needed.

Feed what you learn back. Tell our marketing lead and training team what buyers ask for, what objections come up, and which messages land.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

A proven enterprise closer. Five or more years of full-cycle B2B sales. You have closed deals in the $50,000 to $250,000+ range with multi-stakeholder buying groups at large companies. You sourced a meaningful share of your own pipeline instead of only working inbound leads. Experience selling services, training, consulting, or software to product, technology, or learning leaders is a strong plus.

A strong, personal writer. You write every outreach email yourself, and it shows. Your messages are specific, well researched, and worth a senior executive's time.

Executive presence. You are comfortable on the phone and on video with senior leaders, including on cold calls.

AI in your workflow, without the slop. You use AI tools to research accounts, prepare for calls, and organize your pipeline. You do not use them to mass-produce messages.

Comfortable with a customizable offer. You can sell something shaped to each client without overpromising, and you know when to bring in an expert.

Self-directed. There is no sales manager above you. Experienced product leaders on our team can join calls, review proposals, and help with strategy. But you own your pipeline and your number.

Near-native English, C2 minimum. Written and spoken. You will speak and write directly to senior US enterprise leaders.

Available for US-aligned hours, and able to travel to the US. You need consistent overlap with US business hours. You also need a valid US visa, or the ability to get one, for occasional travel to events and client meetings.

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling corporate training, professional education, or learning and development programs
  • Familiarity with product management and how product teams work
  • A network of product, technology, or AI leaders at US enterprises
  • Experience selling into healthcare or other regulated industries
  • Experience at a boutique consultancy or on a small, early sales team

Benefits

  • Engagement type: 1099 contractor
  • Location: Fully remote, LATAM
  • Working hours: US timezone overlap required
  • Compensation: Monthly retainer of USD 3,000–5,000 plus commission, paid as client payments are collected.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions tohundreds of thousands of businessesand empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Strategic Account Executive.

About the job

This position is needed to sell into high value prospects and customers. This person will play a key role in further growing the business across EMEA with a particular focus on Southern Europe. The candidate will be responsible for managing fast growing customers in the region. Focused mainly on Product cross and up-sell and GP growth, as well as sourcing net new opportunities within a set of accounts.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Servicing the fastest growing customers in the region.
  • Growing our revenue and gross profit share of wallet within your key account list.
  • Opening doors to the purchase of Twilio’s products and services - including voice, messaging, email, contact centre, account security software.
  • Maintaining the highest levels of customer satisfaction.
  • Create pricing proposals, negotiating terms and managing the contract process.
  • Selling solutions to a technical and business audience.
  • Building trust and mutual respect with technical customers and peers.
  • Thinking outside of the box and having extraordinary interpersonal and communication skills to make complex contractual, technical, and financial details sound simple.
  • Balancing challenging priorities and handling multiple projects/deals at the same time.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • Native or bilingual proficiency in both English and Hebrew
  • 6+ years of Account Management/Sales experience covering selling and closing complex technical solutions to a large customer base.
  • History of working with accounts ranging from large multinational enterprise customers to SMB.
  • Demonstrated success by achieving quota on a consistent basis.
  • Track record of Account Management experience and a solid understanding of how to cross sell and upsell solutions within a mature customer base.
  • A solid understanding of financial reporting within a direct customer base - Revenue and Gross Profit tracking, Risk and Opportunity (net new business) cadence.

Desired:

  • Ideally, you also have experience selling both to a business and technical audience.
  • Experience and understanding of working in the communications market is preferable. Have sold or worked with Messaging, Voice Calling, Email, Account Security Verification. Or have prior experience in a traditional telecommunications environment/business.

Location

The position will be based in the United Kingdom, Spain or Ireland

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately 25% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @ email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.

.

Twilio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

jobs.description:
Work From Anywhere in San Fransisco

Work Schedule: PST | Flexible hours with US overlap

About Pearl Talent

Pearl works with the top 1% of candidates from around the world and connects them with the best startups in the US and EU. Our clients have raised over $5B in aggregate and are backed by companies like OpenAI, a16z, and Founders Fund.

Hear why we exist, what we believe in, and who we're building for:
Watch here:

About the Client

A venture-backed healthcare AI company that keeps clinics connected to their patients after every visit is looking for a Head of Patient Experience to build and scale its patient navigation organization.

The company pairs AI-powered workflows with human navigators who follow up on recovery, answer care-plan questions, flag when more care is needed, and book the next appointment. Its platform already runs across hundreds of care locations in more than 15 US states, and patient demand currently outpaces the team's capacity.

About the Role

Reporting directly to the CEO, the Head of Patient Experience owns patient engagement, outreach, and care coordination, and leads the navigator team behind them. The role works closely with product and engineering to decide how AI and navigators share the work as volume grows, and sets HIPAA standards for all patient-facing activity. Success means a scalable navigation organization with sustained gains in engagement, scheduling, and patient satisfaction within 6 to 12 months.

Core Responsibilities

Team Leadership

  • Hire, onboard, and train patient navigators as outreach volume grows.
  • Run QA, coaching, and performance management for the navigation team.
  • Standardize training, QA, and performance management within the first 90 days.
  • Draft and execute a staffing and scaling plan for the navigation organization.

Patient Journey & Engagement

  • Improve the patient journey across outreach, scheduling, and follow-up.
  • Remove access barriers and standardize escalation paths for complex cases.
  • Refine call and SMS scripts and run A/B tests to lift engagement and conversion.
  • Analyze where patients drop off and fix the steps that lose them.

Performance & Reporting

  • Set baselines for contact rate, scheduling rate, CSAT, call quality, and navigator productivity in the first 30 days.
  • Build and maintain dashboards that track these metrics for leadership.
  • Report progress against baselines and recommend process changes.

Product & Compliance

  • Partner with product and engineering on navigator tooling, CRM workflows, and AI automation.
  • Define when AI hands a patient conversation off to a human navigator.
  • Set and enforce HIPAA privacy and compliance standards for all patient-facing work.

Requirements

Must-Have

  • 4+ years in healthcare operations, patient navigation, patient access, or care coordination
  • 2+ years managing patient-facing teams, including hiring, training, QA, and performance management
  • Built or scaled a high-volume patient engagement or care coordination program, including playbooks, call and SMS scripts, training, and QA
  • Hands-on experience building KPI dashboards and running process improvements using metrics such as contact rate, scheduling rate, CSAT, and call quality
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA requirements for patient-facing operations and PHI handling
  • C1+ English (CEFR) for daily work with a US-based CEO, product team, and patients

Nice-to-Have

  • Healthcare technology, centralized navigation, or outbound patient engagement experience
  • Referral completion, enrollment, or call-center coaching experience
  • Startup operations experience with AI automation and CRM tools
  • Experience serving Medicare, Medicaid, or other complex-needs patient populations
  • Prior role at a value-based care or tech-enabled care delivery company

Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: Based on experience and skills
  • Remote Work: Fully remote—work from anywhere
  • Team Incentives: Recognition for maintaining 100% CRM hygiene and on-time reporting
  • Generous PTO: In accordance with company policy
  • Health Coverage for PH-based talents: HMO coverage after 3 months for full-time employees
  • Direct Mentorship: Guidance from international industry experts
  • Learning & Development: Ongoing access to resources for professional growth
  • Global Networking: Connect with professionals worldwide

Our Recruitment Process

  1. Application
  2. Screening
  3. Skills Assessment
  4. Topgrading Interview
  5. Client Interview
  6. Job Offer
  7. Client Onboarding

Ready to Join Us?

If you’re empathetic, organized, and passionate about improving patient experiences through operational excellence, this role is for you. Apply now to help make specialized healthcare more accessible to patients across the U.S.

jobs.excerpt: About Inspira Education Inspira Education Group is one of the fastest-growing edtech startups in the US.
jobs.description:
About Inspira Education

Inspira Education Group is one of the fastest-growing edtech startups in the US. We started with a simple mission to democratize access to high-quality coaching so that every student in the world has an equal opportunity to access the best opportunities.

As the world’s leading network of top admissions coaches in medical, legal, business, and college studies, we’re building software and services in one place—disrupting long-entrenched application processes with products and experiences that strive to provide an equal platform for candidates from diverse backgrounds worldwide.

As one of the fastest-growing edtech firms in the world, we are backed by some of the leading venture capital firms and investors in the world, including Zeev Ventures, Quiet Capital, Craft Ventures and Jeff Fluhr (Founder of Stubhub).

The Role

We’re currently hiring Senior Academic Advisors across multiple Inspira Education Group brands.

We’re looking for a driven, entrepreneurial Senior Academic Advisor with a strong ownership mindset. Someone who thrives in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment and is eager to help students achieve their academic dreams. You’ll play a key role in driving revenue growth through inbound sales, while also helping to build and refine the systems and processes that will allow our sales function to scale in the future.

jobs.title: Account Executive
jobs.excerpt: We are looking for an Account Executive to turn the meetings our SDRs book into signed customers.
jobs.description:
We are looking for an Account Executive to turn the meetings our SDRs book into signed customers. You pick up a prospect who has agreed to a conversation but has not yet decided they want the product, work out how Kaiko fits their operation, show them, and carry it through to a signed pilot. Our buyers are technical, conservative and relationship-driven, so the work is in understanding how they run their fleet well enough to be credible.

Tasks

  • Take the meetings our SDRs book: Read the handover notes and come to the first call already knowing the company, the fleet, and what prompted the conversation.

  • Run discovery that finds the real problem: Ask the uncomfortable second and third question. Understand how the prospect runs inspections, reporting and vetting today, and what it costs them when it goes wrong. Disqualify early when the fit is not there, because a clean no in week one saves everyone a quarter.

  • Demo the product yourself: You run your own demos, with no sales engineer beside you. Know the platform well enough to build the demo around the prospect’s fleet, their problems and their vocabulary, and to answer the hard technical questions in the room.

  • Write and defend the commercial proposal: You put together the pricing, scope, timeline and terms, and then you stand behind them. Be ready to explain how you got to the number and to hold it when the buyer pushes.

  • Build a pipeline of your own: The SDRs will keep meetings coming, and you add to them through referrals, conferences, and the accounts in the CRM that have gone quiet.

  • Stay close after signature: Stay useful through the pilot and afterwards, and grow the account into expansion, references and introductions.

  • Feed the market back into the company: You sit closest to the buyer. Objections, competitor moves, missing features and pricing pushback reach product and leadership while they are still relevant.

  • Improve how we sell: Process, CRM discipline, materials and playbooks, as we grow within the UniSea Group.

What good looks like in your first six months

  • Month 1: You can run a full demo on your own, and you understand how a ship manager operates: inspections, vetting, PSC and the reporting chain. You know enough that a superintendent can talk to you in their own terms.

  • Month 2: You are running first meetings yourself and getting prospects to a second conversation.

  • Month 3: Anyone can look at your pipeline and understand it. Every open opportunity has a named problem, a decision process and a date against it, and the team can build a quarter’s forecast from what you have recorded.

  • Month 4–5: You have taken deals through to proposal on your own, and when you lose one you can say why, specifically enough that we change something as a result.

  • Month 6: You have closed your first paid pilot and handed it over cleanly, and you are hitting your targets month after month.

Requirements

  • At least 2 years closing B2B SaaS or technical solutions, carrying and hitting your own quota.

  • You are comfortable with outbound. You will pick up the phone to someone who has never heard of us, and you treat a quiet week as your own problem to solve.

  • You run your own demos, and you will learn a product deeply enough to be credible in front of a technical superintendent or a fleet manager with twenty years behind them.

  • You have commercial judgment. You can build a proposal, explain a pricing model, and negotiate without conceding the things that matter.

  • You keep your CRM current without being asked. If it is not in the CRM it did not happen, and your forecast holds up.

  • You have resilience and self-direction. Sales cycles are long, the industry is conservative, and you will work your region largely on your own.

  • Maritime, logistics, industrial or other complex B2B experience is an advantage.

  • You speak fluent English. Additional languages relevant to your region are an advantage.

  • You can work remotely with discipline, your working day overlaps substantially with Central European Time, and you are willing to travel for conferences and customer visits.

What we offer

  • A clear path forward, and the honesty to help you take it. You own your region from the start, and we are clear about what the step up to larger accounts asks for. You will hear how you are doing early and directly, while the feedback is still useful, because that is how we work with each other.

  • Direct access to the people who make decisions. We are a small team inside a larger group, so what you learn in the market reaches the people who can act on it.

  • The backing of the UniSea Group, which means the stability and reach of a larger maritime software business behind a team that still moves quickly.

  • Regular team time together and company events.

Change Lead (Contract)

At Connect Centric, we are more than just consultants—we are partners committed to our clients' success. Our hands-on approach means we work closely with our clients to turn strategies into measurable, real-world results. As a strategy execution team, we take full ownership of every initiative from start to finish, so our clients see tangible results, not just ideas.

Position Description

Connect Centric is seeking a Change Lead to lead organizational change management (OCM) for the membership and relationship management workstream of our client's enterprise membership platform implementation. This is a hands-on role that carries change work through every stage of the implementation, from planning and design through testing, go-live and hypercare.

The Change Lead works alongside the client's project leadership, functional teams and implementation partners to understand how the new platform changes the way people work, prepare staff for those changes, and make sure the new processes and tools are adopted and sustained after launch.

What You Will Do

Change Strategy and Planning

  • Develop and maintain the OCM plan and roadmap for the membership and relationship management workstream.
  • Conduct stakeholder analysis and identify, assess and track change risks throughout the implementation.
  • Lead change impact identification, assessment and validation, and keep the change impact tracker current as configuration, testing and project decisions evolve.
  • Update change impacts and mitigation plans as the project moves from design to build, testing and deployment.

Stakeholder Engagement and Communications

  • Plan and develop communications, including functionally targeted communication packages for the teams most affected by the change.
  • Design and facilitate workshops, and document and act on their outputs.
  • Create engagement materials that build awareness, understanding and support across stakeholder groups.
  • Assess stakeholder readiness at key points and adjust engagement approaches accordingly.

Training and Readiness

  • Shape the training strategy, including learner analysis and curriculum design, in partnership with the training team.
  • Support the development, review and validation of training content and materials.
  • Develop learner-support materials for training delivery and the transition to the new platform.
  • Conduct testing and organizational readiness assessments ahead of deployment.

Go-Live, Adoption and Transition

  • Prepare adoption measures and track adoption through go-live.
  • Provide change support during go-live and hypercare.
  • Assess resistance, develop mitigation strategies and update them as adoption findings come in.
  • Report adoption findings and prepare transition documentation so the organization can sustain the change after the engagement ends.

Reporting and Governance

  • Prepare executive reporting on change progress, readiness, risks and adoption.
  • Provide regular OCM status and governance reporting to project leadership.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • 7+ years of experience in organizational change management.
  • Experience leading OCM for at least one enterprise system implementation from planning through go-live and hypercare.
  • Proven experience with change impact assessments, stakeholder analysis and change risk management.
  • Experience planning and producing communications for multiple audiences, including executives.
  • Experience partnering with training teams on training strategy, curriculum and content validation.
  • Experience measuring readiness and adoption and managing resistance.
  • Strong workshop facilitation skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust across functional teams and leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prosci, ACMP (CCMP) or similar change management certification.
  • Experience with membership organizations, associations or nonprofits.
  • Experience with association management system (AMS) or CRM implementations.

Position Details

  • Position Type: Contract, full time Hourly W-2
  • Duration: December 2026 through November 2027
  • Location: Remote
  • Pay Rate: $60/hour - $60 - $65/hour

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are Flosum is a bootstrapped, profitable B2B SaaS company building the leading Salesforce-native DevSecOps, Data Protection, and Security platform.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Flosum is a bootstrapped, profitable B2B SaaS company building the leading Salesforce-native DevSecOps, Data Protection, and Security platform. Our solutions are trusted by Fortune 500 enterprises in the most heavily regulated industries on the planet — financial services, healthcare, government, and insurance.

We’re not a startup burning cash and chasing vanity metrics. We’re a proven, scaling business that reached profitability on our own terms. As a Salesforce Summit Partner and Innovation Award winner, we’ve earned our seat at the table alongside the biggest names in enterprise software.

Built 100% on the Salesforce platform. Serving enterprises that demand zero compromise on security, compliance, and reliability.

Why This Role Exists

We are entering an aggressive growth phase — expanding our product surface, deepening our platform capabilities, and accelerating our delivery velocity. We need senior-caliber Node.js developers who can own significant parts of our architecture and ship production code that enterprise customers depend on daily.

This is not a staff augmentation seat. You will work directly with engineering leadership, product managers, and the CEO. Your decisions will have real consequences, your opinions will be heard, and your craftsmanship will be visible to the customers who rely on our platform.

What You’ll Build

  • High-performance backend services and APIs powering enterprise-grade SaaS applications
  • Scalable, secure Node.js micro services and integrations within the Salesforce ecosystem
  • Modern front-end experiences using Vue.js and TypeScript that serve demanding enterprise users
  • CI/CD pipeline tooling, automation frameworks, and developer productivity infrastructure
  • Real-time data processing and event-driven architectures handling sensitive enterprise data at scale

Requirements

Read this section carefully. We are specific about what we need because we are serious about who we hire.

Non-Negotiable Technical Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional Node.js development in production environments — not tutorials, not side projects, not bootcamp exercises. Real production systems serving real users at scale.
  • Expert-level understanding of asynchronous programming, event loops, streams, and the Node.js runtime. You should be able to explain backpressure, the differences between setImmediate and process.nextTick, and why unhandled promise rejections are dangerous — without Googling it.
  • Deep experience with TypeScript in production codebases. We write typed code, and we expect you to understand why.
  • Strong command of RESTful API design, authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT), and API security best practices for enterprise environments.
  • Proven experience with SQL and NoSQL databases, query optimization, data modeling, and understanding the performance implications of schema decisions at scale.
  • Proficiency with Git workflows, code review practices, automated testing (unit, integration, and end-to-end), and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Solid understanding of containerization (Docker), cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure), and infrastructure-as-code principles.

Highly Preferred (These Will Set You Apart)

  • Salesforce development experience: Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Visualforce, or Salesforce API integrations. If you know both Node.js and Salesforce, you are a rare and extremely valuable candidate to us.
  • Experience building or contributing to Salesforce ISV (AppExchange) products.
  • Vue.js front-end development experience, particularly with Vue 3 Composition API and state management.
  • Experience working in B2B SaaS companies serving enterprise customers with strict compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR).
  • Familiarity with DevOps/DevSecOps toolchains and practices in the Salesforce ecosystem.

The Kind of Person We’re Looking For

Skills get you in the door. Mindset determines whether you thrive here:

Missionary, Not Mercenary

You care about what you’re building and why. You take ownership not because someone assigned it to you, but because that’s who you are. When something is broken at 2 AM, you don’t check whether it’s “your responsibility” — you fix it.

Builder, Not a Bystander

You don’t wait for perfect specifications. You dig in, ask hard questions, propose solutions, and ship. You would rather have a working prototype by Friday than a polished slide deck by next quarter.

Craftsperson Under Pressure

Enterprise customers depend on our uptime and data integrity. You write code that doesn’t just work — it survives. You understand that in regulated industries, your code is your reputation.

Direct Communicator

You say what you think, respectfully and clearly. If a technical decision is wrong, you speak up — regardless of who made it. We value candor over politeness-at-the-expense-of-quality.

This Is a Long-Term Commitment

Let us be direct: we are not looking for contractors who jump between projects every few months. We are building a world-class engineering team, and we invest heavily in the people who join us. In return, we expect commitment.

This role is designed as a long-term, full-time engagement. You will grow with us. You will own systems end-to-end. You will see the direct impact of your work in how Fortune 500 companies build, protect, and deploy on Salesforce.

If you’re looking for a short-term gig while you wait for something else, this isn’t the role. If you want to build something that matters and be part of a team that’s scaling from strong to dominant, keep reading.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with your experience and impact
  • Direct collaboration with the founding team and engineering leadership — your voice will carry weight from day one
  • A profitable, stable company with aggressive growth plans — no funding anxiety, no runway clock
  • The opportunity to work on enterprise-grade products used by some of the largest organizations in the world
  • Meaningful technical challenges: security, compliance, scale, and reliability at the intersection of Node.js and Salesforce
  • A culture that rewards ownership, speed, and craftsmanship over politics and hierarchy
  • Remote-first flexibility with a results-oriented work environment

The Platform Operations Lead will own the operational lifecycle of transactions on Tangible's platform, from listing through to final execution. The role covers deal setup on the platform, preparation and launch of liquidity windows, support through bidding and award, and execution through closing, settlement and fee collection.

As transaction volumes and our partner network grow, the Platform Operations Lead will drive the continued development of our operating model, refining processes, standardising partner playbooks and shaping the platform tooling that supports scale.

jobs.description:
Hiring Entity: FlexEnergi, a Subsidiary of Accurant

Location: Remote

Salary Range: 3,700,000 - 5,500,000 INR

Job Title: Engineering Lead - Grid & Devices (IoT / Energy Systems)

We are hiring an Engineering Lead to own FlexEnergi’s Grid & Devices area end to end: how our DERMS platform connects to devices, which grid standards we speak, and how we dispatch flexible energy resources in real time. It’s the most technically demanding part of our platform and the one our utility customers look at first.

This is a lead role first and a management role second. Expect roughly 70% hands-on technical ownership (architecture, building, code review, and running production systems) and 30% leading a small team of 2–4 engineers. It’s ideal for a senior engineer who wants to be accountable for a critical area, not step away from the code.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the technical direction for Grid & Devices and write the technical plan the team builds from
  • Own the real-time dispatch engine running in production: its design, reliability, and extension to new device types, portfolio-level dispatch, and grid-aware constraints
  • Own the connector architecture and our growing library of device integrations: OEM cloud APIs, aggregator platforms, and direct-to-device protocols
  • Lead our path to OpenADR, IEEE 2030.5 / CSIP, BACnet, Modbus, and OCPP/OCPI compliance and certification, including buy-vs-build decisions on protocol stacks
  • Expand the platform from residential devices into commercial and industrial (C&I) equipment: building management systems, HVAC, batteries, and generators
  • Write code, review code, and set the engineering standards that keep a growing integration library maintainable
  • Own production health for your area (observability, failure handling, runbooks) together with our platform and DevOps engineers
  • Work with product, solution architecture, and utility operations to turn customer requirements into scoped, sequenced engineering work, and push back when needed
  • Lead and grow a small team of engineers: 1:1s, feedback, day-to-day prioritization, and hiring as the team grows
  • Taking ownership of FlexEnergi’s production dispatch engine and evolving it for new device classes
  • Bringing standards-based grid protocols (OpenADR, IEEE 2030.5) into the platform
  • Extending device support to batteries and commercial building systems
  • Grid-aware dispatch that respects feeder and transformer constraints
  • Taking ownership of FlexEnergi’s production dispatch engine and evolving it for new device classes
  • Bringing standards-based grid protocols (OpenADR, IEEE 2030.5) into the platform
  • Extending device support to batteries and commercial building systems
  • Grid-aware dispatch that respects feeder and transformer constraints

Requirements

Required:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience (backend-focused)
  • Deep, hands-on experience with device integration, IoT, or real-time control systems in production: DER, EV charging, smart metering, building automation, industrial IoT, or similar
  • Has owned a production system end to end: designed it, shipped it, supported it, and improved it
  • Strong experience with distributed, event-driven systems: queues and streams, retries and idempotency, time-series data, and devices that are slow, flaky, or offline
  • Strong experience with .NET (C#), or deep experience in Java, Go, or similar and willing to work in .NET
  • Experience as a technical lead, setting direction for a team and raising the bar through design and code review
  • Clear written communication and comfort working async across time zones

Preferred:

  • Most of your career at product companies, building and running your own product rather than delivering client projects
  • Hands-on experience with OpenADR (2.0b / 3.1), IEEE 2030.5 / CSIP, BACnet, Modbus, or OCPP, or with certification testing for any of them
  • Experience with OEM or aggregator APIs for EVs, chargers, thermostats, or batteries
  • Experience with Azure (Event Hub, Service Bus, Functions, Container Apps) and Postgres / Citus
  • Understanding of grid and power-system concepts: demand response, DERMS, feeder and transformer constraints
  • Early-stage or startup experience owning scope that wasn’t fully defined

About Us

FlexEnergi is solving some of the toughest challenges facing today’s utilities. À propos de Workleap

Workleap est une entreprise tech montréalaise fondée en 2006. Bâtisseurs dans l'âme, on crée des produits simples qui font une réelle différence pour ceux qui les utilisent. On a deux lignes de produits : Workleap, conçue pour aider chaque gestionnaire à être plus efficace et ShareGate, la référence mondiale de migration et de gouvernance Microsoft 365. Plus de 15 000 entreprises dans le monde nous font confiance pour faire exactement ça. On est intentionnels dans notre choix des gens qu'on recrute : des personnes qui ont envie de retrousser leurs manches et de construire quelque chose de significatif dans une des périodes les plus excitantes de l'histoire de la tech.

Ton rôle

ShareGate évolue vers des expériences plus modernes, intuitives et fiables, et tu vas aider à mener ce virage. Tu vas bâtir et faire évoluer notre frontend React et TypeScript, influencer l'architecture et l'orientation technique, et travailler avec les équipes produit et design pour régler des problèmes complexes qui comptent pour les client.e.s. Tu vas aussi élever la barre technique par ton jugement, des pratiques modernes et le développement assisté par l'IA au quotidien.

Ton impact :

  • Livrer des fonctionnalités de grande qualité en React et TypeScript qui offrent aux client.e.s de ShareGate des expériences intuitives, rapides et fiables.
  • Façonner l'architecture frontend (composants réutilisables, structure du code, tests, performance) pour que le produit reste facile à maintenir et que chaque nouvelle fonctionnalité sorte plus vite que la précédente.
  • Prendre en charge des initiatives, de la conception technique à la livraison, avec le produit et le design, pour régler de vrais problèmes client.
  • Améliorer en continu la qualité, l'accessibilité, la performance et l'expérience utilisateur, et réduire la dette technique pour que le produit évolue de façon durable.
  • Utiliser chaque jour des outils de développement assisté par l'IA, comme Claude Code, pour livrer plus vite, rehausser la qualité du code et faire progresser les pratiques d'IA de l'équipe.
  • Élever la barre technique de l'équipe par du mentorat, du partage de connaissances et des revues de code qui font grandir les autres.

Ton équipe

Tu vas faire partie de l'équipe ShareGate Migrate, aux côtés de développeur.euse.s d'expérience, d'un.e gestionnaire de produit et d'un.e designer de produit. Tu peux aussi compter sur des expert.e.s de niveau staff et d'autres équipes pour le soutien technique. Dans les 6 à 12 prochains mois, on va améliorer et étendre notre frontend React, peaufiner l'expérience utilisateur et poser les bases techniques de la prochaine étape de ShareGate. On valorise l'autonomie, le sens des responsabilités et la communication ouverte : les décisions techniques se prennent ensemble, les connaissances se partagent et le développement assisté par l'IA fait partie de notre façon de livrer. Notre stack : React et TypeScript, C#/.NET, Azure, API Microsoft Graph, Entra ID, GitHub, tests automatisés et CI/CD.

Ce que tu apportes

  • 5 ans ou plus d'expérience en développement logiciel, idéalement dans un environnement orienté produit ;
  • Une solide expertise en React et TypeScript, avec une bonne maîtrise de l'architecture frontend, de la conception de composants, de la performance et des tests automatisés ;
  • Un jugement technique solide et l'envie de bâtir : tu prends les choses en main, tu décides avec l'information que tu as et tu continues d'élever la barre, côté produit comme côté pratiques d'ingénierie ;
  • Une utilisation quotidienne d'outils d'IA (p. ex. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) en développement logiciel, bien ancrée dans tes habitudes ;
  • Une communication claire et directe, y compris la capacité de remettre en question des décisions produit de façon constructive ;
  • La maîtrise de l’anglais est requise, car tu vas collaborer régulièrement avec des collègues, des clients et des partenaires qui parlent une autre langue que le français ;
  • Atout : expérience en développement backend C#/.NET et avec des API Microsoft comme Microsoft Graph, Entra ID et MSAL.

La plupart de cela te ressemble ? Postule.

Ce que le poste inclut

  • Salaire de base : 125 000 $ – 160 000 $. Cette fourchette reflète notre échelle salariale pancanadienne. L'offre finale peut être ajustée selon la région de la personne candidate pour s'aligner avec les conditions du marché local.
  • Programme de bonus annuel.
  • Programme LTIP, participation à la croissance à long terme de Workleap.
  • REER + Assurances collectives familiales + télémédecine + budget bien-être annuel.
  • Politique de vacances flexible.
  • Télétravail, avec accès à nos bureaux de Montréal.
  • Rassemblement en personne deux fois par an.
  • Claude accessible à tous.

Ce qui nous anime

Chez Workleap, on construit des logiciels au cœur de l'expérience de travail, au quotidien, à tous les niveaux.

On avance vite. Les priorités évoluent, les décisions se prennent avec l'information qu'on a, et on itère. Si tu carbures à l'intensité et que l'ambiguïté ne te fait pas peur, tu vas te sentir chez toi. On est des bâtisseurs. On fait ce qu'il faut pour avancer. L'IA fait partie de l'arsenal. On l'utilise pour aller plus vite et décider plus intelligemment, pas pour remplacer le jugement.

Si tu veux de l'impact réel et un endroit où tes décisions comptent, c'est ici.

Comment on recrute

La transparence, c'est notre façon de recruter — pour toi comme pour nous.

Voici comment ça se passe : un premier échange avec un.e recruteur.euse, puis un entretien virtuel avec le.la gestionnaire d'embauche. Tu complètes ensuite une étude de cas à faire chez toi, suivie d'une rencontre avec de futur.es collègues pour en discuter ensemble. Selon le poste, le parcours peut varier légèrement — ton.ta recruteur.euse t'en donnera tous les détails lors de votre premier appel.

On utilise l'IA pour soutenir certaines étapes du processus, mais chaque décision d'embauche reste humaine.

On a hâte de te rencontrer.

You'll work at the intersection of engineering and software—connecting data from multiple systems, building robust data models, and creating reporting solutions that help municipal water utilities better understand and manage their infrastructure.

If you enjoy solving complex data challenges, building high-quality reporting systems, and turning technical requirements into intuitive visualizations, we'd love to hear from you.

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

Responsibilities:

Full-Stack Developer – Next.js & Python

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote

Working Hours: U.S Business Hours

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Full-Stack Developer to build and maintain production web applications across a modern frontend, backend, database, and cloud stack.

This is a hands-on development role for someone who can own a slice of the product across both UI and API. You’ll work with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, relational and graph databases, multi-service architecture, real-time functionality, and Azure infrastructure.

What You’ll Own

Frontend Development

  • Build production web applications using Next.js 16 with App Router, React 19, and strict TypeScript.
  • Work with server/client boundaries and data-fetching using TanStack Query or equivalent.
  • Build interfaces using Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui + Radix, Zustand, React Hook Form + Zod, and AG Grid Enterprise.
  • Work with Framer Motion and Socket.IO.
  • Write frontend tests using Vitest + Testing Library.
  • Build end-to-end tests using Playwright.

Backend Development

  • Build and maintain backend services using Python 3.13 and FastAPI.
  • Work with Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2 / SQLModel, Alembic, Celery, Redis, and uv.
  • Work with typed schemas, async I/O, authentication, and background jobs.
  • Work within a multi-service codebase using HTTP between services, Redis, and workers.

Database & Data

  • Work with relational modeling and migrations using SQLAlchemy/Alembic or equivalent.
  • Work with Azure SQL (MSSQL) and PostgreSQL.
  • Work with Neo4j for family / heirship graphs.
  • Work with PostgreSQL + pgvector.
  • Work with MongoDB for logs.

Cloud & Operations

  • Work with Azure services including Blob, Identity, Key Vault, SQL, and Container Registry.
  • Work with Docker Compose.
  • Work with Prometheus / Grafana.
  • Work with pnpm workspaces + Turborepo.

Advanced Features & Integrations

  • Work with graph databases or non-trivial graph UIs such as trees, canvases, XYFlow/D3/canvas.
  • Work with complex data UIs including AG Grid, maps, PDF viewers, and rich text using Tiptap.
  • Work with real-time technologies such as Socket.IO / WebRTC or telephony platforms such as Telnyx or similar.
  • Work with LLM/RAG features including embeddings, pgvector, and tool-using assistants.
  • Work with chatbot services; you do not need to be an ML engineer.

Required Experience & Skills

  • 6+ years shipping production web apps.
  • 3+ years as the person who owns a slice across UI and API.
  • Strong TypeScript and React experience.
  • Comfortable with App Router, server/client boundaries, and data-fetching using TanStack Query or equivalent.
  • Strong Python and FastAPI experience, or Django/Flask at a similar depth.
  • Experience with typed schemas, async I/O, authentication, and background jobs.
  • Strong relational modeling and migration experience using SQLAlchemy/Alembic or equivalent.
  • Experience with MSSQL or PostgreSQL.
  • Experience in a multi-service codebase with HTTP between services, Redis, and workers, not only a single monolith.
  • Tests as a habit: unit/integration on the backend and component tests on the frontend.
  • Clear written communication.
  • Ability to leave the next engineer a module they can change without a walkthrough.

Strongly Preferred

  • Graph databases such as Neo4j or non-trivial graph UI using trees, canvases, XYFlow/D3/canvas.
  • Azure experience with SQL, Blob, Key Vault, or a comparable cloud.
  • Experience with complex data UIs such as AG Grid, maps, PDF viewers, or rich text using Tiptap.
  • Real-time experience with Socket.IO / WebRTC or telephony with Telnyx or similar.
  • LLM/RAG experience including embeddings, pgvector, and tool-using assistants.

Nice-to-Haves We Actually Use

  • WebRTC calling.
  • DocuSign / PKCS#7 signing.
  • GEDCOM.
  • Google Maps.
  • Campaign/inbox graph models.
  • Prometheus metrics.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You have extensive experience shipping production web applications and owning a slice across both UI and API.
  • You’re comfortable working across TypeScript/React and Python/FastAPI.
  • You can confidently reason about relational modeling, migrations, and multi-service architecture.
  • You’re comfortable working with Redis, workers, and HTTP communication between services.
  • You treat testing as part of development rather than something to add later.
  • You communicate clearly in writing.
  • You leave the next engineer with a module they can change without a walkthrough.

What Success Looks Like

  • You can independently own a slice of the product across UI and API.
  • Production features are supported by appropriate backend and frontend tests.
  • Relational models and migrations are reliable and maintainable.
